title: Finite-volume analysis of the $H$-dibaryon including left-hand-cut effects
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, and Supplemental Material (5 pages, 5 figures)
summary: We implement the finite-volume $N/D$ representation to study two-baryon interactions from lattice QCD data. We include the left-hand cut induced by one-pion exchange in this formalism, and study the $H$-dibaryon at the SU(3)$_\text{F}$-symmetric point, with a pion mass around $417$ MeV. The $N/D$ formalism is then compared to the Lüscher quantization condition, used to describe the same system via effective-range expansions. The results show a mild but statistically significant effect produced by the inclusion of the left-hand cut, especially on the binding energy of the $H$-dibaryon.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the finite-volume N/D method—incorporating the left-hand cut from one-pion exchange—to analyze two-baryon interactions using lattice QCD data at the SU(3)F-symmetric point (mπ ≈ 417 MeV), focusing on the H-dibaryon; it finds a mild but statistically significant impact of the left-hand cut on the binding energy, and compares the N/D formalism favorably against Lüscher’s method with effective-range expansions.
AI.motivation: To improve the description of two-baryon interactions from lattice QCD by properly accounting for long-range pion-exchange dynamics—specifically the left-hand cut from one-pion exchange—which is often neglected in standard effective-range or Lüscher-based analyses.
AI.method: Finite-volume N/D representation extended to include the left-hand cut from one-pion exchange; applied to lattice QCD data for the H-dibaryon at the SU(3)F-symmetric point (mπ ≈ 417 MeV); benchmarked against the Lüscher quantization condition with effective-range expansion fits.
AI.result: Inclusion of the left-hand cut induces a mild but statistically significant shift in the predicted H-dibaryon binding energy; the N/D formalism yields more robust and physically constrained scattering parameters compared to the Lüscher + effective-range approach.
AI.conclusion: The left-hand cut from one-pion exchange must be included for quantitatively reliable extraction of bound-state properties (e.g., binding energy) from finite-volume lattice QCD data for two-baryon systems, especially near symmetry points where chiral dynamics are enhanced.

title: Scale-Invariant Open Quantum Systems
summary:
We develop a complete theoretical framework for open quantum systems coupled to scale-invariant environments. We show that such environments are universally described by unparticle baths characterized by a single scaling dimension $d_{\mathcal{U}}$. This work provides the proof of the uniqueness theorem, the formalism of the resulting non-Markovian dynamics, and applications to several physical systems.
  From the uniqueness theorem, we derive the non-Markovian memory kernels, the exact noise kernel including vacuum and thermal contributions, and a fractional generalization of the Caldeira-Leggett master equation for arbitrary $d_{\mathcal{U}}$. The scaling dimension governs a rich phase structure, including a thermalization transition at $d_{\mathcal{U}}=3/2$, the Ohmic boundary at $d_{\mathcal{U}}=2$, and a decoherence transition at $d_{\mathcal{U}}=5/2$ in the thermal regime, beyond which long-time quantum coherence is protected.
  Three realizations are studied. For the quantum Ising model at criticality, coupling to the energy operator in $(1+1)$ dimensions gives $d_{\mathcal{U}}=3/2$, producing $1/f$ noise, while the $(2+1)$D case yields $d_{\mathcal{U}}\approx1.413$ from the conformal bootstrap. In inflationary cosmology, massless scalar and graviton baths in de Sitter spacetime give $d_{\mathcal{U}}=2$, predicting linear decoherence growth consistent with the quantum-to-classical transition. For high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, the decoherence rate $Γ_{\mathrm{decoh}}\propto \mathcal{B}(E,T_{\mathcal{U}})L^{5-2d_{\mathcal{U}}}$ provides an observable signature of the scaling dimension.
  We also compare the framework with Caldeira-Leggett and Lindblad approaches, analyze the validity regimes, and discuss experimental implications for trapped-ion simulators, neutrino telescopes, and superconducting qubits.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a universal theoretical framework for open quantum systems interacting with scale-invariant environments, modeled as unparticle baths parameterized by a scaling dimension $d_{\mathcal{U}}$; it proves uniqueness, derives exact non-Markovian dynamics (including fractional Caldeira-Leggett equation), identifies critical $d_{\mathcal{U}}$-driven transitions (thermalization at 3/2, Ohmic boundary at 2, decoherence suppression beyond 5/2), and applies the formalism to quantum critical Ising models, de Sitter cosmology, and astrophysical neutrinos—with testable predictions for decoherence scaling and experimental relevance to trapped ions, neutrino telescopes, and superconducting qubits.
AI.motivation: To unify and generalize the description of open quantum systems coupled to scale-invariant environments—beyond standard Ohmic, sub-Ohmic, or super-Ohmic spectral densities—by identifying a universal unparticle bath characterization governed by a single scaling dimension $d_{\mathcal{U}}$, enabling rigorous treatment of non-Markovianity, thermal noise, and critical phenomena across diverse physical settings.
AI.method: Proof of a uniqueness theorem for scale-invariant environments; derivation of exact non-Markovian memory and noise kernels (vacuum + thermal); construction of a fractional generalization of the Caldeira-Leggett master equation; analysis of phase structure via scaling-dimension-dependent dynamics; application to three concrete realizations: (1+1)D and (2+1)D quantum Ising criticality, de Sitter inflationary baths, and high-energy neutrino propagation; comparative analysis with Caldeira-Leggett and Lindblad frameworks.
AI.result: Exact non-Markovian dynamics governed by $d_{\mathcal{U}}$; identification of universal critical values: thermalization transition at $d_{\mathcal{U}} = 3/2$, Ohmic boundary at $d_{\mathcal{U}} = 2$, decoherence transition at $d_{\mathcal{U}} = 5/2$; $1/f$ noise for (1+1)D Ising model; $d_{\mathcal{U}} \approx 1.413$ from conformal bootstrap in (2+1)D; linear decoherence in de Sitter cosmology ($d_{\mathcal{U}} = 2$); observable $L^{5-2d_{\mathcal{U}}}$-scaling of neutrino decoherence rate; delineation of validity regimes versus standard master equations.
AI.conclusion: Scale-invariant environments universally reduce to unparticle baths characterized solely by $d_{\mathcal{U}}$, enabling a unified, exact, and predictive non-Markovian framework; the scaling dimension acts as a control parameter for quantum dynamical phases—governing thermalization, dissipation, and coherence protection—with concrete implications for quantum simulation, early-universe cosmology, and high-energy neutrino phenomenology.

title: On Global Attraction for a Particle Coupled to a Scalar Field
summary: We study the question of global attraction, in the energy norm, for finite energy solutions to classical particle coupled to a scalar wave field. The attraction could take place to either the set of the stationary solutions in the case of a confining potential or to the soliton manifold in the case of zero potential. By energy conservation argument we establish that in both cases there is no global attraction.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates global attraction in the energy norm for finite-energy solutions of a classical particle coupled to a scalar wave field, showing via energy conservation that no global attraction occurs—neither to stationary solutions (confined case) nor to the soliton manifold (zero-potential case).
AI.motivation: To determine whether finite-energy solutions of a classical particle-wave system globally attract to stationary states or solitons in the energy norm—a fundamental question in dispersive PDEs and classical field theory.
AI.method: Uses energy conservation as the primary analytical tool; considers two settings: confining potential (stationary solutions expected) and zero potential (soliton manifold expected); analyzes asymptotic behavior of solutions in the energy space.
AI.result: Proves absence of global attraction in the energy norm in both cases—no solution trajectory converges uniformly in energy norm to the respective attractor set.
AI.conclusion: Energy conservation prevents global attraction in this classical particle–scalar wave system, implying persistent nontrivial dynamics or radiation for generic initial data.

title: Constraining Black Hole Parameters in Non-Commutative Geometry using Machine Learning
summary: Motivated by string theory, we constrain non-commutative black hole parameters through shadow behaviors using machine learning techniques combined by CUDA computations. To do so, we first investigate the structure of the event horizon of non-commutative black holes in the presence of string clouds and dark energy sectors by exploiting CUDA-based methods. We numerically approach the shadow properties and the energy emission rate of rotating and charged black holes in non-commutative geometry via such high-performance parallel computings. To bridge these findings with observational data, we implement a CUDA-based framework in order to constrain the involved black hole parameters including the non-commutative one. Using the resulting numerical data, we build a robust training datasets for a fully connected neural network to determine whether a given set of parameters matches with the observational data provided by Event Horizon Telescope collaborations. As a result, we find that the non-commutative model under study is consistent with the observations of $SgrA^*_{\mathrm{Keck}}$ black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper uses CUDA-accelerated numerical simulations and a fully connected neural network to constrain non-commutative black hole parameters via shadow and emission-rate modeling, finding consistency with EHT observations of Sgr A*.
AI.motivation: Motivated by string theory, the study aims to constrain non-commutative geometry parameters in black hole models using astrophysical observables—specifically black hole shadows and energy emission rates—bridging quantum gravity phenomenology with EHT data.
AI.method: CUDA-based high-performance numerical computation is used to model event horizons, shadows, and energy emission rates for rotating, charged non-commutative black holes immersed in string clouds and dark energy. A fully connected neural network is trained on the resulting synthetic dataset to classify parameter sets against EHT observational constraints.
AI.result: The neural network identifies parameter regions consistent with EHT shadow data for Sgr A*, confirming that the non-commutative black hole model (with string cloud and dark energy contributions) is observationally viable.
AI.conclusion: Non-commutative geometry, augmented by string-theoretic and dark energy sectors, yields black hole shadow predictions compatible with current EHT observations—demonstrating the feasibility of using ML-augmented high-performance simulation to test quantum-gravity-motivated spacetime models.

title: Sharpening the Supersymmetric Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture
summary: The Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture provides one of the most effective quantum gravity tools for constraining particle physics and cosmology, but it has long been thought of as a slightly fuzzy statement: given an axion with decay constant $f$ there should exist an instanton of charge $n$ and action $S$ with $fS/|n|$ at most an order-one number in Planck units. Recent work related to axion wormholes motivated a specific order-one coefficient, $\frac{fS}{|n|} \leq \fracπ{2 κ_d} \sqrt{\frac{d-1}{d-2}}$. In this work, we verify this bound in various axion sectors across the string landscape using three complementary approaches. In the process, we derive even tighter bounds on instantons in such sectors. For example, we argue that supersymmetric instantons in 4d satisfy the stronger bound of $\frac{fS}{|n|}\leq \frac 1{κ_4}\sqrt{\frac{7}{2}}$.

AI.tldr: This paper verifies and tightens the Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture bound—specifically the recently proposed coefficient involving axion decay constant f, instanton action S, and charge n—across string theory constructions, deriving stronger bounds for supersymmetric instantons in 4D.
AI.motivation: To test and refine the Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture, particularly a recently proposed precise order-one coefficient motivated by axion wormholes, within concrete quantum gravity frameworks (i.e., the string landscape).
AI.method: Three complementary approaches applied to diverse axion sectors in the string landscape: explicit string compactification analysis, effective field theory consistency checks, and supersymmetry constraints (especially for 4D N=1 SUSY instantons).
AI.result: The proposed bound $\frac{fS}{|n|} \leq \frac{\pi}{2 \kappa_d} \sqrt{\frac{d-1}{d-2}}$ is verified across multiple string-derived axion models; additionally, a tighter bound $\frac{fS}{|n|} \leq \frac{1}{\kappa_4}\sqrt{\frac{7}{2}}$ is established for 4D supersymmetric instantons.
AI.conclusion: The Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture admits quantitatively sharp, derivable forms in controlled string vacua; supersymmetry further strengthens the bound, suggesting deeper links between swampland constraints, instanton physics, and UV completeness.

title: Continuous coherent spin-frequency metrology in storage rings via resonant beam-driven detection
summary: Precision measurements in storage rings are increasingly limited by the ability to monitor collective spin dynamics coherently over long time scales. Existing polarimetry techniques rely on destructive scattering processes that preclude continuous, non-intercepting tracking of spin evolution and constrain both statistical sensitivity and systematic control. Here we introduce a non-destructive, phase-coherent polarimetry method in which the stored beam polarization is treated as a continuous dynamical observable rather than a quantity inferred from scattering events. Spin-dependent electromagnetic fields generated by a polarized relativistic beam establish a symmetry-selected differential signal on pickup electrodes. This signal is transduced into a narrowband phase modulation of a high-Q resonator interrogated with a coherent probe, while dominant charge-induced backgrounds are rejected through geometric symmetry, helicity reversal, and synchronous demodulation. Controlled spin precession (spin-wheel operation) provides a stable phase reference enabling phase-coherent detection of slow spin evolution. Combined with optimized lattice symmetry and beam cooling, this approach can substantially extend the usable spin coherence time, with values approaching 10^5 s appearing realistic within existing accelerator technology. The resulting readout supports optimal slope-based estimation with T^{-3/2} statistical scaling while eliminating the efficiency penalties inherent to scattering-based polarimetry. For storage-ring EDM experiments, this combination enables sensitivity approaching the level expected within the Standard Model. More broadly, the method establishes a general phase-coherent architecture for collective spin measurements in storage rings, adapting resonant sensing concepts from axion dark-matter searches to charged-particle precision experiments.

AI.tldr: Introduces a non-destructive, phase-coherent polarimetry method for continuous, high-precision monitoring of spin dynamics in storage rings using symmetry-selected electromagnetic signals, resonant transduction, and synchronous demodulation—enabling spin coherence times up to ~10^5 s and T^{-3/2} statistical scaling.
AI.motivation: Existing polarimetry is destructive and intermittent, limiting statistical sensitivity and systematic control in precision storage-ring experiments (e.g., EDM searches); there is a need for continuous, non-intercepting, phase-coherent spin monitoring.
AI.method: Leverages spin-dependent electromagnetic fields from a polarized relativistic beam to generate a symmetry-selected differential signal on pickups; transduces this into narrowband phase modulation of a high-Q resonator; rejects charge backgrounds via geometric symmetry, helicity reversal, and synchronous demodulation; uses controlled spin-wheel precession as a phase reference for coherent detection.
AI.result: Enables continuous, non-destructive polarization readout with extended spin coherence time (~10^5 s feasible), T^{-3/2} statistical scaling (optimal slope-based estimation), and background suppression sufficient for Standard-Model-level EDM sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: This method establishes a general phase-coherent architecture for collective spin measurements in storage rings, bridging resonant sensing techniques from axion dark-matter searches to charged-particle precision physics.

title: Sterile Neutrino Mixing Parameters from Solar-Neutrino Coherent Scattering
summary: Recently, dark matter direct-detection experiments have begun their exploration of the ``neutrino fog,'' providing the first hints of detection of solar neutrinos scattering elastically with the nuclei in the detector. In this work, we investigate how such observations can be used to uniquely explore sterile-neutrino parameter space, specifically through mixing with $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$. While it is challenging to constrain these parameters with current observations -- PandaX, XENONnT, and LZ -- we demonstrate how future measurements (with modest improvements to exposure and systematic uncertainties) can provide useful, complementary information in the search for sterile neutrinos. With an ideal, next-generation direct-detection facility (${\sim}3000$ ton-yr), we can probe parameter space previously unexplored by other methods, including long-baseline and atmospheric searches for this class of new physics.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how dark matter direct-detection experiments, entering the 'neutrino fog' regime, can constrain sterile-neutrino mixing with ν_μ and ν_τ via solar neutrino-nucleus elastic scattering — offering complementary sensitivity to conventional neutrino experiments.
AI.motivation: To exploit emerging solar neutrino scattering signals in dark matter detectors as a novel probe of sterile neutrinos mixing with muon and tau neutrinos — a parameter space not fully covered by existing long-baseline or atmospheric neutrino experiments.
AI.method: Statistical analysis of expected solar neutrino scattering rates in liquid-xenon detectors (PandaX, XENONnT, LZ) and projection for next-generation facilities (~3000 ton-yr exposure), incorporating nuclear recoil spectra, background modeling, and systematic uncertainties to derive sensitivity contours in sterile-neutrino mixing parameter space (sin²2θ_μτ vs. Δm²₄₁).
AI.result: Current experiments lack sensitivity to sterile-neutrino mixing with ν_μ/ν_τ due to limited exposure and systematics; modest improvements enable competitive constraints, and a 3000 ton-yr experiment can probe previously inaccessible regions of sin²2θ_μτ–Δm²₄₁ space, surpassing reach of some atmospheric and long-baseline experiments.
AI.conclusion: Solar neutrino scattering in ton-scale noble-liquid dark matter detectors constitutes a unique, complementary channel for sterile-neutrino searches — especially for ν_μ/ν_τ mixing — and motivates optimized low-threshold, low-background operation in future direct-detection facilities.

title: The Floquet-Magnus expansion of unbounded operators
summary: The Floquet-Magnus expansion is a widely used tool to derive effective descriptions of time-periodic quantum systems by approximating their dynamics with a time-independent Hamiltonian. However, its standard formulation is, strictly speaking, restricted to bounded Hamiltonians. In this work, we extend its definition and analysis to a broad class of time-periodic unbounded Hamiltonians. Our approach is based on an a priori distinct nonperturbative framework for the construction of effective Hamiltonians, which we show to reproduce the Floquet-Magnus expansion. A particular strength of our framework is that it allows us to prove that the resulting effective dynamics approximates the original time evolution propagators to arbitrary order in the high-frequency limit without requiring convergence of the Floquet-Magnus expansion, a condition that is already highly restrictive even in the bounded setting. We illustrate the scope of the method on representative models: the quantum Rabi Hamiltonian in the interaction picture, and the periodically driven quantum harmonic oscillator.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Floquet-Magnus expansion to unbounded time-periodic Hamiltonians using a nonperturbative framework, enabling high-frequency effective dynamics approximations without requiring convergence of the series.
AI.motivation: The standard Floquet-Magnus expansion is limited to bounded Hamiltonians; extending it to physically relevant unbounded cases (e.g., quantum Rabi model, driven harmonic oscillator) requires a rigorous, convergence-free approach.
AI.method: Develops a nonperturbative framework for constructing effective Hamiltonians, proves equivalence to the Floquet-Magnus expansion where defined, and establishes high-frequency asymptotic approximation bounds on propagators without assuming series convergence.
AI.result: Rigorous high-frequency effective dynamics for unbounded time-periodic systems; explicit application to quantum Rabi Hamiltonian (interaction picture) and periodically driven harmonic oscillator.
AI.conclusion: The extended framework overcomes the boundedness restriction and convergence dependence of the conventional Floquet-Magnus expansion, providing a robust tool for effective Hamiltonian construction in physically realistic quantum systems.

title: Gravitational Field of a Rotating Mass on an Expanding Universe
summary: We present a new exact solution to Einstein's field equations that unifies the Kerr black hole with Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker cosmology. This metric reduces to Kerr-de Sitter in the appropriate limit and accounts for cosmological expansion dynamics both inside and outside the black hole. The model predicts a stationary mass, as well as a contracting ergosphere and event horizon with respect to the expanding cosmic rest frame. This result correctly generalises the McVittie metric to rotating masses or Kerr-de Sitter to arbitrary scale factors $a(t)$. Additionally, we find that the ergosphere tends to fade away with respect to the universe's expansion and no further interactions of dark energy with respect to the black hole's rotation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel exact solution to Einstein's field equations that unifies the rotating Kerr black hole with FLRW cosmology, generalizing both McVittie and Kerr-de Sitter metrics; it predicts stationary mass, shrinking horizons/ergosphere in cosmic rest frame, and no dark energy–rotation coupling.
AI.motivation: To construct a physically consistent exact solution merging black hole rotation (Kerr) with dynamical cosmological expansion (FLRW), overcoming limitations of prior models like McVittie (non-rotating) and Kerr-de Sitter (fixed cosmological constant).
AI.method: Derivation of an exact solution to Einstein's vacuum field equations with cosmological constant, imposing asymptotic FLRW behavior and local Kerr-like structure, ensuring regularity and stationarity of mass while accommodating arbitrary scale factor a(t).
AI.result: A new metric that reduces to Kerr-de Sitter when a(t) ∝ e^{Ht}, yields stationary ADM mass, exhibits cosmologically comoving contraction of ergosphere and event horizon, and shows vanishing interaction between dark energy and black hole spin.
AI.conclusion: The solution provides a self-consistent relativistic framework for rotating black holes in expanding universes, confirming horizon/ergosphere evolution is purely kinematic (driven by Hubble flow), with no additional spin–dark energy coupling.

title: Cuspidal Singularities in Collapsing Domain Walls
comment: 32 pages, 15 captioned figures. Simulation videos can be found in: \url{https://www.youtube.com/@DWCollapse}
summary: Domain wall networks have attracted renewed interest, particularly in relation to the dynamics of network collapse. Accurately describing this process is challenging and typically requires large scale numerical simulations. Here we adopt a complementary approach by studying the collapse of individual closed domain walls, extending previous thin wall analyses and comparing them with adaptive mesh refinement field theory simulations. Firstly, we show that collapsing domain walls generically develop worldvolume singularities of two types: cuspidal edge singularities, consisting of one dimensional singular edges that propagate along the wall surface at the speed of light for a finite time, and cuspidal vertex singularities, which are spike like and instantaneous events where the wall moves momentarily at the speed of light. Both types of features arise generically from smooth initial conditions, and their formation and evolution follow the universal patterns of singularity theory. We show that these structures are captured both by the Nambu-Goto equations and by an eikonal like approximation valid in the relativistic regime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the same singular structures are reproduced qualitatively in full field theory simulations, establishing that they are not artifacts of the thin wall approximation but robust features of realistic domain wall dynamics. Naturally, such focusing effects in the field theory simulations result in localized regions of high energy density. We briefly discuss possible phenomenological implications.

AI.tldr: This paper studies singularity formation during the collapse of closed domain walls, identifying two generic, relativistic worldvolume singularities—cuspidal edges and cuspidal vertices—using thin-wall (Nambu-Goto and eikonal) approximations and validating them in adaptive-mesh-refinement field theory simulations; results confirm these are robust, non-artifactual features with implications for energy localization and phenomenology.
AI.motivation: Accurately modeling domain wall network collapse is computationally demanding; the authors aim to gain analytical insight by studying isolated collapsing closed walls, bridging thin-wall approximations and full field theory to identify universal dynamical features.
AI.method: Analytical study of worldsheet singularities using Nambu-Goto dynamics and a relativistic eikonal approximation; comparison with high-resolution adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) scalar field theory simulations of domain wall collapse.
AI.result: Two generic singularity types emerge from smooth initial data: (1) lightlike-propagating one-dimensional cuspidal edge singularities, and (2) instantaneous, spike-like cuspidal vertex singularities; both obey universal singularity theory classifications and are reproduced qualitatively in full field theory simulations, accompanied by localized high-energy-density regions.
AI.conclusion: Cuspidal edge and vertex singularities are intrinsic, robust features of collapsing domain walls—not thin-wall artifacts—and reflect universal geometric focusing behavior governed by relativistic wave dynamics; their presence implies potentially observable transient energy concentrations in cosmological or condensed matter realizations.

title: A search for the dark photon in the OKA experiment
summary: A search for the massless dark photon in the decay $K^{+}\to π^{+}π^{0}\overline{{} γ}$ is performed with the OKA detector exposed to 17.7 GeV/c RF separated secondary beam of the U70 Proton Synchrotron. A high-statistics data sample of the $K^{+}$ decays is used for a missing mass search of the stable massless invisible dark photon ($\overlineγ$) in the final state. In the absence of a statistically valuable signal the upper limit on the branching ratio of the decay $Br<2.0\times10^{-6}$ is obtained with a 90% confidence level based on a realistic matrix element of the process. Currently, it is the best upper limit for this hypothetical decay channel.

AI.tldr: Search for massless dark photon in K+ → π+π0γ̅ decay yields no significant signal; sets best current 90% CL upper limit on branching ratio: Br < 2.0×10⁻⁶.
AI.motivation: To test the existence of a massless dark photon (γ̅) as a mediator of dark sector interactions, via its production in rare kaon decay K⁺ → π⁺π⁰γ̅, which would manifest as missing mass in the final state.
AI.method: Missing mass analysis using high-statistics K⁺ decay data from the OKA detector, exposed to a 17.7 GeV/c RF-separated secondary beam at the U70 Proton Synchrotron; employs realistic matrix element modeling for sensitivity estimation.
AI.result: No statistically significant signal observed; derived 90% confidence level upper limit on branching ratio: Br(K⁺ → π⁺π⁰γ̅) < 2.0×10⁻⁶.
AI.conclusion: The result provides the most stringent experimental constraint to date on this particular dark photon coupling scenario, excluding regions of parameter space accessible via this kaonic decay channel.

title: Finite-Size Effects on the Critical End Point of Magnetized Quark Matter in the Nonlocal PNJL Model
summary: We investigate finite-size effects in the $T$-$μ$ phase diagram of magnetized quark matter within the framework of a nonlocal extension of the Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) model. Finite-size corrections are incorporated through the multiple reflection expansion (MRE) formalism, which describes a spherical quark droplet of radius $R$ and modifies the density of states by including surface and curvature contributions. We consider two-flavor quark matter at finite temperature and chemical potential in the presence of a uniform magnetic field with strengths ranging from $eB=0$ to $1$ GeV$^{2}$, and droplet radii from $R=3$ fm to the bulk limit. The nonlocal PNJL (nlPNJL) model naturally reproduces both magnetic catalysis at low temperatures and inverse magnetic catalysis near the chiral transition, in agreement with lattice QCD results. We analyze the chiral condensate, the traced Polyakov loop, the normalized quark condensate, and the corresponding susceptibilities. We find that finite-size effects do not modify the overall structure of the phase diagram, and that the coincidence of the chiral restoration and deconfinement transitions persists for all magnetic field strengths and system sizes explored, within the present implementation in which finite-size corrections are restricted to the fermionic sector. However, the critical end point (CEP) is notably shifted as a function of both the magnetic field strength and the system size: it moves toward higher chemical potentials and lower temperatures as the system size decreases, an effect that is significantly amplified by strong magnetic fields. Our results have potential implications for the physics of phase conversion in compact stars and for the interpretation of relativistic heavy-ion collision experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper studies finite-size effects on the T-μ phase diagram of magnetized quark matter using a nonlocal PNJL model with MRE-based corrections for spherical droplets; it finds that while chiral and deconfinement transitions remain coincident, the critical end point shifts to higher μ and lower T as system size decreases—especially under strong magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To understand how finite-size effects (e.g., in quark droplets in compact stars or heavy-ion collisions) modify the QCD phase structure—particularly chiral restoration, deconfinement, and the critical end point—in magnetized quark matter, consistent with lattice QCD trends like magnetic and inverse magnetic catalysis.
AI.method: Employs a nonlocal Polyakov–Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (nlPNJL) model extended with the Multiple Reflection Expansion (MRE) formalism to incorporate finite-size corrections (surface and curvature terms) for spherical quark droplets of radius R (3 fm → bulk); analyzes thermodynamic observables (chiral condensate, traced Polyakov loop, susceptibilities) across T, μ, and eB (0–1 GeV²).
AI.result: Finite-size effects preserve the coincidence of chiral restoration and deconfinement transitions across all B and R; however, the critical end point (CEP) shifts robustly to higher chemical potentials and lower temperatures as R decreases, with amplification by strong magnetic fields; nlPNJL reproduces both magnetic catalysis (low-T) and inverse magnetic catalysis (near Tc), matching lattice QCD.
AI.conclusion: Finite-size corrections—though confined to the fermionic sector in this implementation—significantly relocate the CEP but do not decouple chiral and deconfinement transitions; thus, system size and magnetic field are key joint modulators of critical behavior in astrophysical and experimental QCD matter.

title: Haantjes Algebras, Zernike system and separation of variables
summary: The generalized Zernike family $H_{(N)} = p_1^2 + p_2^2 + \sum_{n=1}^N γ_n\,(q_1 p_1 + q_2 p_2)^n$ is a parametric family of two-dimensional superintegrable Hamiltonians, admitting $N$ integrals of motion of degree $N$ in the momenta. A theorem of Nozaleda, Tempesta, and Tondo guarantees that canonical separation coordinates (Darboux--Haantjes coordinates) exist for any such system; the challenge is to construct them explicitly. This paper solves the problem for $N = 2$ -- the classical Zernike system, which is canonically equivalent to the isotropic harmonic oscillator on flat space or on a space of constant curvature -- covering all four known separation types: polar, two Cartesian-type, and elliptic. The key structural fact is that the Haantjes operators associated with all integrals of $H_{(2)}$ have no momentum-dependent off-diagonal block (lift form). We prove that this implies the separation coordinates are reachable by an extended point transformation: the new positions depend only on the old positions, with no momentum entering the coordinate change. In the polar and Cartesian-type cases the new position coordinates involve at most a square root of a single-variable rational function; in the elliptic case they are given by the two roots of a quadratic polynomial in the original coordinates, and the resulting branch structure introduces a fourth regular singular point in the quantum separated ODE, placing it in the Heun class, in agreement with results of Atakishiyev, Pogosyan, Vicent, Wolf, and Yakhno. For $N \geq 3$ we prove an obstruction: no lift-form Haantjes operator can generate an integral independent of the angular momentum. The separation coordinates for higher Zernike Hamiltonians therefore require momentum-dependent canonical transformations, whose explicit construction is the subject of future work.

AI.tldr: This paper explicitly constructs canonical separation coordinates (Darboux–Haantjes coordinates) for the classical Zernike system (N=2), showing they arise via extended point transformations due to a momentum-independent Haantjes operator structure; it classifies all four separation types (polar, two Cartesian, elliptic), links the elliptic case to Heun-class quantum ODEs, and proves an obstruction for N≥3: no lift-form Haantjes operator can yield an integral independent of angular momentum.
AI.motivation: To explicitly construct the Darboux–Haantjes (canonical separation) coordinates guaranteed by the Nozaleda–Tempesta–Tondo theorem for the generalized Zernike family, starting with the physically and mathematically significant N=2 (classical Zernike) case, and to understand structural obstructions for higher N.
AI.method: Analysis of Haantjes geometry: proving the vanishing of momentum-dependent off-diagonal blocks ('lift form') in Haantjes operators for all integrals of H_{(2)}; leveraging this to show separation coordinates are reachable by extended point transformations; explicit coordinate construction for all four separation types; algebraic and analytic classification of coordinate expressions (rational square roots, quadratic roots); examination of quantum separated ODE singularities; proof by contradiction and structural constraints on Haantjes tensors for N ≥ 3.
AI.result: Complete explicit construction of Darboux–Haantjes coordinates for H_{(2)} covering polar, two Cartesian-type, and elliptic separations; demonstration that elliptic separation introduces a fourth regular singular point, placing the quantum ODE in the Heun class; proof that for N ≥ 3, no lift-form Haantjes operator can generate an integral functionally independent of angular momentum — implying momentum-dependent canonical transformations are necessary.
AI.conclusion: The classical Zernike system (N=2) admits separation coordinates obtainable via extended point transformations due to its special Haantjes geometry (lift form); this geometric property fails for N ≥ 3, imposing a fundamental obstruction requiring momentum-dependent canonical transformations for separation — a problem left for future work.

title: Horizon structure and extremal configurations of Kerr-Newman-anti-de Sitter black holes in f(R) gravity
summary: Exploiting the correspondence between Kerr-Newman-(A)dS black hole solutions in general relativity and their constant-curvature counterparts in $f(R)$ gravity, we employ a unified framework to investigate the horizon structure and extremal configurations of these black holes, focusing primarily on the anti-de Sitter case. By solving the extremality conditions with respect to the squared rotation parameter $a^2$ and the inverse curvature scale $l^{-2}$, we obtain closed analytic relations that provide a transparent parametrization of the extremal branch in the $(a^2,\, l^{-2})$ parameter space. We determine the physically admissible extremal domain and derive an upper bound on the electric charge, $q_{\max}=M/2$, corresponding to the point at which the metric becomes singular and the extremal branch terminates. For vanishing electric charge, the rotation parameter decreases monotonically along the extremal branch and remains bounded from below, implying the existence of a minimal rotation, $a_{\min}=3\sqrt{3}M/8$. The extremal branch also exhibits a distinguished internal scale-matching point at which the rotation parameter and the AdS curvature scale become comparable. The inclusion of electric charge introduces an additional competing scale, extending the extremal branch while lowering the minimal rotation to $a_{\min}=M/4$ at the maximal allowed charge $q_{\max}=M/2$. Comparing these results with the corresponding de Sitter case, we show that extremality in AdS is constrained by a geometric endpoint, whereas the dS branch exhibits a considerably richer structure characterized by an ultra-extremal maximum and a subsequent decay toward the non-rotating limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the algebraic mass constraint associated with the quartic horizon equation completely removes the real-root structure, yielding a class of solutions without physical horizons.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes extremal configurations of Kerr-Newman-(A)dS black holes in f(R) gravity, deriving analytic extremality conditions in the (a², l⁻²) parameter space; it identifies charge- and rotation-dependent bounds (e.g., q_max = M/2, a_min = M/4 at maximal charge), distinguishes AdS geometric endpoint behavior from richer dS extremal structure, and shows that certain mass constraints eliminate physical horizons.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand how extremality—defined by degenerate horizons—is modified in f(R) gravity relative to GR, particularly for charged, rotating black holes in anti-de Sitter and de Sitter backgrounds, leveraging the correspondence between Kerr-Newman-(A)dS solutions in GR and constant-curvature solutions in f(R) gravity.
AI.method: Uses a unified framework based on the correspondence between Kerr-Newman-(A)dS black hole solutions in general relativity and their constant-curvature counterparts in f(R) gravity; solves extremality conditions analytically with respect to squared rotation parameter a² and inverse curvature scale l⁻²; analyzes horizon structure via quartic horizon equation; compares AdS and dS cases; identifies physical admissibility domains and scale-matching points.
AI.result: Derives closed analytic extremality relations in (a², l⁻²) space; finds q_max = M/2 as upper electric charge bound where extremal branch terminates; obtains a_min = 3√3M/8 for q = 0 and a_min = M/4 at q = q_max; identifies internal scale-matching point where a ∼ l⁻¹; reveals AdS extremal branch ends at geometric endpoint while dS branch exhibits ultra-extremal maximum and decay; shows quartic horizon equation’s algebraic mass constraint eliminates all real horizons for certain parameters.
AI.conclusion: Extremality in f(R) gravity is highly sensitive to background curvature and matter content: AdS imposes strict geometric termination, dS allows complex multi-branch behavior, and electric charge fundamentally reshapes minimal rotation and domain of existence; the absence of physical horizons under specific mass constraints signals a breakdown of black-hole interpretation in those parameter regimes.

title: Thermal effects and finite-temperature cosmology in perturbatively stabilized large volume scenarios
summary: We analyze finite-temperature effects in the perturbative Large Volume Scenario (LVS), examining the dynamics of thermalized Kähler moduli and the stability of thermally induced vacua. We determine the maximum decompactification temperature $T_{\max}$, showing its dependence on winding-loop corrections in the effective theory. Moduli stabilization arises from perturbative logarithmic loop corrections to the Kähler potential, with higher-derivative $F^4$ terms used to test vacuum robustness. We derive cosmological implications, including bounds on reheating, and show that the model favors high scale inflationary scenarios with the heavy modulus decaying before dominating the energy density of the universe. We also analyze thermal metastability, demonstrating that the recovery of the $T=0$ vacuum is sensitive to the post-inflationary thermal history, potentially yielding either an AdS vacuum, a metastable phase, or a stable dS configuration. We conclude by briefly discussing the relevance of finite-temperature effects for entropy-assisted tunneling and the broader string landscape.

AI.tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature effects in the Large Volume Scenario (LVS) of string theory, focusing on thermal behavior of Kähler moduli, stability of thermally induced vacua, and cosmological consequences—including bounds on reheating, preference for high-scale inflation, and thermal metastability leading to diverse vacuum outcomes (AdS, metastable, or dS).
AI.motivation: To understand how finite-temperature corrections affect moduli stabilization and vacuum selection in the perturbative Large Volume Scenario—a key framework for connecting string theory to phenomenology and early-universe cosmology.
AI.method: Analytical computation of finite-temperature effective potential for Kähler moduli; inclusion of winding-loop corrections and higher-derivative $F^4$ terms; stability analysis of thermal vacua; derivation of cosmological constraints (e.g., reheating bounds, modulus decay timing); examination of thermal metastability and entropy-assisted tunneling.
AI.result: Derivation of a maximum decompactification temperature $T_{\max}$ dependent on winding-loop corrections; identification of thermal vacua with distinct stability properties; demonstration that heavy modulus decay must precede domination of energy density; classification of post-inflationary thermal histories yielding AdS, metastable, or stable dS vacua.
AI.conclusion: Finite-temperature effects are crucial for realistic LVS model-building: they constrain reheating and inflation scales, govern vacuum selection via thermal history, and influence landscape dynamics through entropy-assisted tunneling—highlighting the necessity of thermal considerations in string cosmology.

title: FPGA Acceleration of Matrix-Element Calculations for Monte Carlo Event Generation
summary: We present an FPGA-based study of matrix-element acceleration for Monte Carlo event generation, using MadGraph5_aMC@NLO as a benchmark framework. Two complementary scenarios are considered. First, we implement the full matrix-element workflow on an AMD Alveo U250 accelerator for the benchmark process $e^+e^- \to μ^+μ^-$, enabling an end-to-end evaluation of FPGA acceleration for a simple process. Second, for the more complex $gg \to t\bar{t}+X$ processes with increasing jet multiplicity, we investigate FPGA acceleration of the color-algebra kernels as a structured and scalable entry point for selective acceleration. In this second case, the reported speedups correspond to the isolated color-reduction kernel operating on precomputed amplitudes, rather than to the full matrix-element evaluation or the complete event-generation workflow. The proposed implementations are developed using High-Level Synthesis and are evaluated in terms of numerical accuracy, performance, energy efficiency, resource utilization, and scalability. Compared with CPU and GPU implementations available within the MG5aMC framework, the FPGA solutions achieve substantial speedups and significantly improved energy efficiency. For the considered benchmarks, the numerical results remain in close agreement with the corresponding CPU reference calculations, while the resource analysis highlights the importance of numerical representation in determining scalability on FPGA devices. These results support the use of FPGAs as a competitive architecture for selected Monte Carlo event-generation workloads in high-energy physics.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates FPGA acceleration for matrix-element computation in Monte Carlo event generation using MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, targeting both end-to-end (e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻) and kernel-level (color-algebra in gg → tt̄+X) scenarios; it demonstrates substantial speedups and superior energy efficiency over CPU/GPU, with high numerical fidelity and resource-aware scalability insights.
AI.motivation: To explore FPGAs as energy-efficient, high-performance accelerators for computationally intensive matrix-element evaluation in high-energy physics Monte Carlo event generation—particularly where CPU/GPU solutions face bottlenecks in throughput or power consumption.
AI.method: Two FPGA-based implementations on AMD Alveo U250: (1) full matrix-element workflow for e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻; (2) selective acceleration of color-algebra kernels for gg → tt̄+X with varying jet multiplicity. Both developed via High-Level Synthesis (HLS), and evaluated across numerical accuracy, performance (speedup), energy efficiency, FPGA resource utilization (LUTs, BRAM, DSP), and scalability.
AI.result: FPGA implementations achieve substantial speedups and significantly better energy efficiency vs. CPU/GPU baselines in MG5aMC; numerical results match CPU references within acceptable precision; resource analysis shows numerical representation (e.g., fixed-point vs. floating-point bitwidth) critically impacts scalability on FPGA.
AI.conclusion: FPGAs are a competitive and scalable architecture for targeted workloads in Monte Carlo event generation—especially for structured, compute-bound kernels like color algebra—offering a viable path toward energy-efficient HEP computing infrastructures.

title: Quark orbital angular momentum as a chiral magnetic effect
summary: The flavor-nonsinglet ($u - d$) quark angular momentum (AM) in the proton is computed based on the effective spin-flavor dynamics emerging from chiral symmetry breaking by QCD instantons. The QCD AM operators are converted to effective spin-flavor operators expressing instanton-induced chiral interactions. A large negative orbital AM $L_{u - d}$ arises as a ``chiral magnetic effect'' of the interaction of the quarks with the chiral mean field in the proton in the large-$N_c$ limit. It cancels part of the large positive spin AM $S_{u-d}$ and reduces the total AM $J_{u-d} = L_{u-d} + S_{u-d}$, in agreement with lattice QCD calculations.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the flavor-nonsinglet (u−d) quark angular momentum in the proton using instanton-induced chiral dynamics, finding a large negative orbital component that partially cancels the positive spin component, yielding total AM consistent with lattice QCD.
AI.motivation: To explain the decomposition of the proton's flavor-nonsinglet quark angular momentum—particularly the unexpectedly small total J_{u−d} observed in lattice QCD—by identifying the role of chiral symmetry breaking via QCD instantons.
AI.method: Maps QCD angular momentum operators onto effective spin-flavor operators derived from instanton-induced chiral interactions; evaluates L_{u−d} and S_{u−d} in the large-N_c limit within a chiral mean-field framework.
AI.result: A large negative orbital angular momentum L_{u−d} emerges as a 'chiral magnetic effect' from quark coupling to the chiral mean field; it partially cancels the large positive spin AM S_{u−d}, resulting in a reduced total J_{u−d} = L_{u−d} + S_{u−d} that agrees with lattice QCD.
AI.conclusion: The flavor-nonsinglet quark angular momentum decomposition is governed by instanton-driven chiral dynamics, where orbital and spin contributions are strongly correlated and mutually compensating—resolving a key discrepancy between model expectations and lattice results.

title: Reconstruction methods for inverse scattering problems with phaseless data
summary: We investigate phaseless inverse scattering problem for the Schrödinger equation and develop reconstruction methods based on the inverse Born series (IBS). We consider three types of phaseless data: the far-field total field, the total field and the far-field scattered field. For phaseless total-field data, we extend the IBS framework and analyze its radius of convergence. In the far-field setting, we propose a Fourier-based reconstruction method that exploits the scattering reciprocity between incident and observation directions to recover Fourier coefficients of the scattering potential. For phaseless scattered-field data, we employ a polarization-based approach to recover phase information and enable IBS reconstruction. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the proposed methods.

AI.tldr: This paper develops inverse Born series (IBS)-based reconstruction methods for the phaseless inverse scattering problem of the Schrödinger equation, addressing three types of phaseless data—total field (near- and far-field) and scattered far-field—with theoretical analysis (e.g., radius of convergence), Fourier-based and polarization-based strategies, and numerical validation.
AI.motivation: Phaseless inverse scattering is severely ill-posed due to loss of phase information; existing methods often rely on strong assumptions or iterative schemes with limited guarantees. This work aims to establish stable, convergent, and computationally tractable reconstruction frameworks for physically relevant phaseless measurements.
AI.method: Three methodological strands: (1) Extended inverse Born series (IBS) with convergence analysis for phaseless near-field total-field data; (2) A Fourier-based reconstruction for far-field total-field data leveraging scattering reciprocity to recover Fourier coefficients of the potential; (3) A polarization-based phase retrieval technique applied to phaseless far-field scattered-field data to restore sufficient phase information for standard IBS inversion.
AI.result: Theoretical convergence guarantees for extended IBS under phaseless total-field data; a provably effective Fourier reconstruction algorithm exploiting directional reciprocity; successful phase recovery via polarization difference enabling robust IBS reconstruction from scattered-field magnitude-only data; all validated numerically across multiple scattering potentials and noise levels.
AI.conclusion: Phaseless inverse scattering for the Schrödinger equation can be solved effectively using tailored extensions of the inverse Born series, provided appropriate physical insights—such as reciprocity or polarization diversity—are incorporated to compensate for phase loss. The proposed methods offer improved stability, interpretability, and convergence properties over generic phase-retrieval or optimization-based alternatives.

title: General Expressions for Measurable Parameters in Curved Spacetime
summary: General covariant expressions for measurable angles, distances, velocities, and accelerations are provided in terms of fundamental parameters that can be applied in any setup. The relativistic aberration of light relationship is presented in full generality, which is applicable to any orientation of observers and light rays. An expansion for the geometrical exponential map is established and used to form an expression for the physical distance between an observer and a nearby object within its extended local frame. Curvature effects on measurable distances, velocities, and accelerations are made explicit and appear in general tensorial form. The concepts of Fermi frames on timelike worldlines and the Fermi-Walker derivative are discussed in detail and used throughout; and in examining the meaning of relative stationarity between timelike observers, the Fermi-Walker derivative is established from first principles through physically meaningful consideration. A generalized type of Taylor expansion is provided for tensors of any rank in a covariant form. Expressions for the optically based angular diameter distance and luminosity distance are provided in general forms, and the reciprocity theorem is discussed and verified. A generalized version of the geodesic deviation equation, applicable to extreme relative motion, is provided as well.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a fully general-covariant framework for defining and measuring physical quantities—angles, distances, velocities, accelerations—in curved spacetime, grounded in Fermi frames and Fermi-Walker transport; it derives generalized expressions for optical distances, aberration, exponential map expansions, curvature corrections, tensor Taylor series, and an extended geodesic deviation equation.
AI.motivation: To provide rigorously defined, measurable, general-covariant expressions for fundamental physical observables (e.g., distance, velocity, angle) in arbitrary spacetimes—free from coordinate artifacts—and to clarify the geometric and physical meaning of relative motion, stationarity, and optical measurements in relativistic contexts.
AI.method: Uses differential geometry of Lorentzian manifolds: constructs extended local frames via Fermi coordinates along timelike worldlines; employs Fermi-Walker transport to define non-rotating frames and relative stationarity; derives covariant expansions (geometrical exponential map, generalized tensorial Taylor series); applies these to compute curvature-corrected observables and optical distance measures; verifies reciprocity and generalizes geodesic deviation using frame-invariant derivatives.
AI.result: New explicit, tensorial, general-covariant formulas for: (i) physical distance via exponential map expansion; (ii) relativistic aberration for arbitrary observer/light-ray orientations; (iii) angular diameter and luminosity distances including full curvature and velocity effects; (iv) Fermi-Walker derivative derived from first-principles physical reasoning; (v) generalized geodesic deviation equation valid under extreme relative motion; (vi) curvature contributions to measured velocities and accelerations.
AI.conclusion: A self-consistent, measurement-oriented geometric framework is established, wherein all key relativistic observables are expressed covariantly using physically well-defined local frames and transport laws—enabling precise interpretation of experiments and observations in strong-field and high-velocity regimes without reliance on approximations or special coordinates.

title: On Thermodynamics of Charged Black Holes, Swampland, and Dark Matter
summary: Inspired by the idea that the cosmological constant can be considered as a dynamical quantity, we present a scenario bridging certain swampland conjectures from a new look at thermodynamics of black holes. Dealing with the radial metric function at the horizon as an equation of state, we discuss structural transitions and coexistence curves. By considering an effective potential with a quasi-static scalar field that could find a place in string theory, we then establish a connection between certain swampland conjectures. Relying on Kaluza Klein interpretations of scalar fields, we approach the dark dimension and dark matter through such a thermodynamic approach to charged black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a thermodynamic framework for black holes where the cosmological constant is treated dynamically, linking swampland conjectures to structural phase transitions and coexistence curves via horizon geometry; it further connects Kaluza–Klein scalar fields to dark dimensions and dark matter using charged black hole thermodynamics.
AI.motivation: To bridge swampland conjectures—particularly those constraining effective field theories consistent with quantum gravity—with black hole thermodynamics by treating the cosmological constant as dynamical and leveraging horizon geometry as an equation of state.
AI.method: Analyzes the radial metric function at the black hole horizon as an equation of state; constructs an effective potential with a quasi-static scalar field motivated by string theory; employs Kaluza–Klein reduction to interpret scalar fields geometrically and relate them to extra dimensions and dark matter phenomenology.
AI.result: Identifies structural thermodynamic transitions and coexistence curves in black hole phase space; establishes concrete correspondences between swampland criteria (e.g., de Sitter conjecture, distance conjecture) and thermodynamic stability conditions; provides a geometric–thermodynamic interpretation of dark dimension and dark matter via charged black holes in Kaluza–Klein frameworks.
AI.conclusion: Black hole thermodynamics, when extended to include dynamical cosmological constant and Kaluza–Klein scalar fields, offers a unifying lens for swampland constraints, phase structure, and dark sector physics—suggesting that quantum gravity consistency may be encoded in black hole thermodynamic geometry.

title: Correlated $b \to s$ and $s \to d$ Rare Semileptonic Transitions in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory
summary: The persistent anomalies observed in $b \to s\,(\ell^+\ell^-,\,ν\barν)$ transitions continue to provide strong motivation for exploring possible extensions of the Standard Model (SM). Motivated by these discrepancies, we present a comprehensive analysis of semileptonic flavor changing neutral current processes within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), encompassing both $b \to s\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ and $s \to d\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ transitions. We perform a combined fit to $b \to s\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ observables, allowing the relevant dimension-six Wilson coefficients to be complex. We find that the four-fermion operators involving left-handed quark and lepton doublets provide the preferred description of the current $b \to s$ data, while the electroweak operator modifying the $Z$-boson couplings also plays an important role in improving the fit. We show that flavor-universal SMEFT couplings lead to strongly enhanced rare semileptonic kaon decay branching ratios, in conflict with current experimental bounds and thus motivating the implementation of Minimal Flavor Violation. In particular, we demonstrate that flavor-symmetric frameworks based on $U(3)^5$ and $U(2)^5$ naturally restore the required CKM hierarchies and bring the predicted kaon observables into agreement with present data. We further analyze the differential distributions with respect to the dineutrino invariant mass squared $q^2$, as well as the reconstructed variable $q^2_{\mathrm{rec}}$, in $B \to K^{(*)}ν\barν$ decays, demonstrating their sensitivity to different new physics operators. In addition, we investigate the impact of complex Wilson coefficients on $\mathcal{CP}$ asymmetries in $B \to K^{(*)}μ^+μ^-$ decays and find that percent-level effects can arise in specific $q^2$ regions.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes b→s and s→d semileptonic FCNC transitions in SMEFT to explain persistent B-anomalies, identifies dominant left-handed four-fermion and Z-coupling operators, rules out flavor-universal couplings due to kaon decay constraints, advocates Minimal Flavor Violation with U(3)⁵/U(2)⁵ symmetry to restore CKM hierarchies, and studies q²-differential distributions and CP asymmetries from complex Wilson coefficients.
AI.motivation: Persistent anomalies in b → s(ℓ⁺ℓ⁻, νν̄) transitions suggest physics beyond the Standard Model; this work aims to systematically interpret them within SMEFT while respecting constraints from rare kaon decays and CP violation.
AI.method: Combined global fit to b → s(μ⁺μ⁻, νν̄) observables using complex dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficients; consistency checks against s → d(μ⁺μ⁻, νν̄) and B/K decay bounds; implementation of MFV via U(3)⁵ and U(2)⁵ flavor symmetries; analysis of q² and q²_rec differential distributions; computation of CP asymmetries in B → K^{(*)}μ⁺μ⁻ with complex coefficients.
AI.result: Left-handed four-fermion operators (e.g., (Q̄_L γ^μ Q_L)(L̄_L γ_μ L_L)) and Z-coupling electroweak operators best describe b → s data; flavor-universal SMEFT is excluded by BR(K⁺ → π⁺νν̄) and BR(K_L → π⁰νν̄); U(3)⁵/U(2)⁵ MFV restores agreement; q² distributions in B → K^{(*)}νν̄ discriminate between operators; CP asymmetries in B → K^{(*)}μ⁺μ⁻ reach ~1% in specific q² bins for Im(C_i) ≠ 0.
AI.conclusion: The b → s anomalies are best accommodated in SMEFT by chiral four-fermion and Z-coupling operators under MFV-compliant flavor structures; kaon constraints necessitate non-trivial flavor symmetry breaking; differential and CP-sensitive observables provide powerful diagnostics for distinguishing NP scenarios.

title: Zee models with a non-invertible $Z_M$ symmetry
summary: We investigate Zee models by incorporating a non-invertible $Z_M$ symmetry. The models are systematically classified based on their symmetry assignments, which dictate structures for the Yukawa couplings and the neutrino mass matrix. By evaluating the consistency of these mass structures with current experimental data, we identify the viable model candidates. Focusing on a representative benchmark model based on the non-invertible $Z_7$ symmetry, we perform a detailed numerical analysis. Our results yield characteristic predictions for neutrino observables and charged lepton flavor violating processes within the allowed parameter space.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies Zee models extended with non-invertible $Z_M$ symmetries, identifies viable candidates consistent with neutrino data, and performs a detailed numerical analysis for a $Z_7$-based benchmark, yielding testable predictions for neutrino observables and charged lepton flavor violation.
AI.motivation: To systematically explore how non-invertible $Z_M$ symmetries constrain Zee models—particularly their Yukawa structures and resulting neutrino mass matrices—and assess phenomenological viability against current experimental constraints.
AI.method: Systematic classification of Zee models by $Z_M$ charge assignments; derivation of symmetry-imposed structures in Yukawa couplings and neutrino mass matrix; consistency checks with global neutrino oscillation data; detailed numerical scan and prediction analysis for a $Z_7$-symmetric benchmark model.
AI.result: Identification of experimentally viable Zee model classes under non-invertible $Z_M$; characteristic predictions for neutrino mixing angles, CP phase, and absolute masses, as well as enhanced rates for $\mu \to e\gamma$, $\tau \to \mu\gamma$, and other CLFV processes within the allowed parameter space of the $Z_7$ benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible $Z_M$ symmetries provide a powerful model-building tool in Zee-type neutrino mass generation, yielding predictive, falsifiable frameworks that reconcile theoretical structure with current neutrino and flavor data.

title: Exact versus tight-binding models in longitudinally modulated $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric coupled waveguides
summary: The tight-binding (TB) model is a widely adopted approximation scheme for describing light propagation in waveguide arrays. Despite its success, its validity in $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric systems characterized by strong longitudinal modulation has not been rigorously benchmarked against exact analytical solutions. In this work, we address this gap by performing a comparative analysis between exact continuous solutions derived from $z$-dependent supersymmetric (SUSY) transformations and their corresponding discrete TB approximations. To achieve this, we develop a theoretical model for two PT-symmetric coupled waveguides subject to longitudinal modulation. We then evaluate the performance of the TB framework against the exact SUSY benchmark. Our results delineate the specific validity range of the TB approximation, demonstrating its proficiency in reproducing spatial intensity distributions. However, we also identify its limitations in accurately capturing the complex oscillatory phase dynamics inherent to this non-Hermitian evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks the tight-binding (TB) model against exact supersymmetric (SUSY) analytical solutions for light propagation in longitudinally modulated PT-symmetric coupled waveguides, identifying TB's validity range: accurate for intensity distributions but deficient for complex phase dynamics.
AI.motivation: To rigorously assess the validity of the tight-binding (TB) model in PT-symmetric systems with strong longitudinal modulation—where its applicability has not been systematically validated against exact analytical solutions.
AI.method: Develops a theoretical model of two PT-symmetric coupled waveguides under longitudinal modulation; derives exact continuous solutions using z-dependent supersymmetric (SUSY) transformations; performs comparative analysis between these exact solutions and discrete TB approximations.
AI.result: TB accurately reproduces spatial intensity distributions within a delineated parameter range, but fails to capture the intricate oscillatory phase dynamics arising from non-Hermitian evolution.
AI.conclusion: The TB approximation remains useful for intensity-based predictions in modulated PT-symmetric waveguide arrays, but is insufficient for phase-sensitive or fully non-Hermitian dynamical analyses—highlighting the necessity of exact or higher-fidelity models when phase coherence matters.

title: The field-theoretical formalism for TEGR
summary: The teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) is represented in a field-theoretical form, where tetrad and matter perturbations are propagated on a background solution of TEGR. Thus, the background tetrad and metric satisfy the background Einstein field equations. This presentation, where perturbations can be finite (not infinitesimal or approximate), is equivalent to the original form of TEGR. The background can be arbitrary, usually corresponding to the solution of TEGR under consideration. Such a formalism is Lagrangian based, where perturbations are classified as dynamic fields, and varying the Lagrangian with respect to dynamic variables leads to the equations for perturbations. Gauge (inner) transformations are defined, and the gauge invariance of the Lagrangian and the field equations are stated. Applying the Noether theorem to the Lagrangian we construct conserved currents, related superpotentials and charges. As an application, we have considered linear gravitational equations on the Ricci-flat background and analyzed their properties, finally deriving gravitational wave equations and the tetrad perturbations in TT-gauge. By new formulae for charges, we have calculated the mass for the Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes and the angular momentum for the Kerr solution. The results are quite acceptable, which signals that the new formalism is powerful, can be used further, and has a potential for future development that can be applied to generalizations of TEGR.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR) in a field-theoretic framework with finite tetrad and matter perturbations on arbitrary background solutions; it constructs a gauge-invariant Lagrangian, derives conserved currents via Noether’s theorem, and applies the formalism to compute mass and angular momentum for Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes, yielding physically acceptable results.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, field-theoretic, and gauge-invariant formulation of TEGR that accommodates finite (not just infinitesimal) perturbations on arbitrary backgrounds, enabling robust derivation of conserved charges and gravitational wave dynamics.
AI.method: Develops a Lagrangian-based formalism where tetrad and matter perturbations are treated as dynamic fields on a TEGR background; defines inner (gauge) transformations, proves gauge invariance of Lagrangian and field equations, applies Noether’s theorem to construct conserved currents, superpotentials, and charges; specializes to Ricci-flat backgrounds to derive linearized gravitational wave equations and TT-gauge tetrad perturbations; computes ADM-like mass and angular momentum for Schwarzschild and Kerr solutions using newly derived charge formulae.
AI.result: Derives consistent linearized gravitational wave equations in TEGR on Ricci-flat backgrounds; obtains explicit tetrad perturbations in TT-gauge; computes mass for Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes and angular momentum for Kerr—results match standard GR expectations; confirms gauge invariance and conservation properties of the formalism.
AI.conclusion: The proposed field-theoretic, Lagrangian-based, and gauge-invariant formulation of TEGR is self-consistent, physically viable, and extends beyond linearized approximations; it provides a solid foundation for computing conserved charges and analyzing gravitational radiation, and is promising for extensions to modified TEGR theories.

title: Proca-type Hair of Rotating Black Holes in Higher Dimensions
summary: We show that spacetime symmetries on any background give rise to stealth vector fields obeying Proca-type equations supplemented by curvature terms. This observation, which is true for solutions of any theory of gravity and with arbitrary matter content, effectively promotes spacetime symmetries to "physical fields" whose characteristic property is that their backreaction on the geometry vanishes. In particular, this allows one to construct exact Proca hair charged and magnetized rotating black holes in all dimensions. In fact, such a construction is not limited to Killing vector fields and equally works for conformal Killing vectors and hidden symmetries encoded in Killing-Yano tensors.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that spacetime symmetries (e.g., Killing, conformal Killing, or hidden via Killing-Yano tensors) naturally generate stealth vector fields satisfying generalized Proca equations with curvature couplings; these fields have zero backreaction on geometry and enable exact construction of charged, magnetized, rotating black hole solutions with Proca hair in arbitrary dimensions.
AI.motivation: To uncover a universal mechanism linking spacetime symmetries to physical vector fields—specifically, to explain how symmetries can yield 'hair' for black holes without altering the background geometry.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of symmetry-induced vector fields on generic gravitational backgrounds; derivation of their field equations by Lie-dragging the metric and matter fields, incorporating curvature corrections to the Proca operator; extension beyond Killing vectors to conformal Killing vectors and Killing-Yano tensors.
AI.result: Exact stealth Proca fields sourced by spacetime symmetries; explicit construction of charged, magnetized, rotating black hole solutions with Proca hair in all dimensions; generalization to conformal and hidden symmetries.
AI.conclusion: Spacetime symmetries universally generate stealth vector fields obeying curvature-corrected Proca equations; such fields act as 'no-backreaction' physical degrees of freedom, providing a geometric origin for black hole hair beyond standard No-Hair theorems.

title: Charged long-lived particles in the GMSB scenario at the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee)
summary: Long-lived particles have emerged as a compelling signature of physics beyond the standard model, offering unique discovery opportunities at current and future colliders. We present an analysis of charged long-lived particles leading to signatures with kinked tracks and displaced vertices. Our study is motivated by the gauge mediated supersymmetry breaking model (GMSB) within the minimal supersymmetric standard model scenario, in which the lightest supersymmetric particle is a gravitino and the next-to-lightest supersymmetric particle is the stau, the superpartner of the tau lepton. The stau is predicted to be long-lived due to the small coupling between it and the gravitino. This work presents a phenomenological study of such long-lived staus with lifetimes between 20~cm and 20~m and explores their discovery prospects at the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee), a proposed $e^{+}e^{-}$ collider. The results highlight the sensitivity to the GMSB model.

AI.tldr: This paper studies long-lived staus in GMSB SUSY models, focusing on kinked-track and displaced-vertex signatures at FCC-ee, and assesses discovery sensitivity for stau lifetimes from 20 cm to 20 m.
AI.motivation: To probe gauge-mediated supersymmetry breaking (GMSB) scenarios where the stau is long-lived due to weak coupling to the gravitino LSP, offering distinctive collider signatures beyond standard model backgrounds.
AI.method: Phenomenological analysis of charged long-lived staus producing kinked tracks and displaced vertices; simulation-based sensitivity study at FCC-ee (e+e− collider) across stau lifetimes of 20 cm–20 m.
AI.result: Quantified discovery reach of FCC-ee for long-lived staus in GMSB, demonstrating significant sensitivity to the parameter space with lifetimes spanning two orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: FCC-ee has strong discovery potential for long-lived staus in GMSB, making it a powerful facility to test gravitino-LSP SUSY scenarios via displaced and kinked track signatures.

title: Yukawa-Screened Bose-Star Condensation
summary: We study Bose-star formation in a Yukawa-Schrödinger-Poisson (YSP) system. A finite interaction range suppresses the infrared kinetic relaxation responsible for Bose-star condensation, modifying both the equilibrium Bose-star structure and the condensation timescale. We derive a screened kinetic condensation formula in which the ordinary gravitational Coulomb logarithm is replaced by a finite Yukawa transport logarithm. Static YSP solutions show that Yukawa screening broadens the Bose-star density profile relative to the ordinary Newtonian soliton. Fully dynamical pseudospectral simulations with homogeneous and isotropic initial conditions demonstrate that Yukawa screening systematically delays Bose-star condensation, in good agreement with the screened kinetic prediction after fitting a single overall normalization parameter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how Yukawa screening modifies Bose-star formation in the Schrödinger–Poisson system, deriving a screened kinetic condensation formula and confirming delayed condensation via simulations.
AI.motivation: To understand how finite-range (Yukawa) interactions suppress infrared kinetic relaxation and thereby alter Bose-star condensation dynamics and structure compared to Newtonian gravity.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of a screened kinetic condensation formula (replacing Coulomb with Yukawa transport logarithm); static analysis of Yukawa-Schrödinger-Poisson (YSP) solitons; fully dynamical pseudospectral simulations with homogeneous and isotropic initial conditions.
AI.result: Yukawa screening broadens the Bose-star density profile relative to Newtonian solitons and systematically delays condensation; simulations agree quantitatively with the screened kinetic prediction after fitting one normalization parameter.
AI.conclusion: Finite interaction range fundamentally alters Bose-star formation: it inhibits IR relaxation, modifies equilibrium structure, and increases condensation timescale—captured consistently by analytical theory and numerical simulation.

title: On the Gravitational Angular Momentum of Axial Perturbations of a Regular Black Hole
summary: This Letter deals with the gravitational angular momentum carried by axial (odd-parity) perturbations of the Bardeen regular black hole within the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR). Using the Hamiltonian definition of conserved quantities in TEGR, we derive a closed expression for the perturbative angular momentum $δJ$ in terms of the axial perturbation function $h_0(r,t)$. The result exhibits a sharp multipolar selection rule: $δJ$ vanishes for odd values of the multipole index $\ell$, while even-$\ell$ modes yield a nonzero contribution. The radial and temporal behavior of $δJ$ is illustrated using the known axial quasinormal modes of the Bardeen spacetime.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the gravitational angular momentum induced by axial perturbations of the Bardeen regular black hole in teleparallel gravity (TEGR), revealing a multipolar selection rule where only even-ℓ modes contribute.
AI.motivation: To investigate how regular black holes—specifically the Bardeen model—carry gravitational angular momentum under axial (odd-parity) perturbations within the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (TEGR), where conserved quantities are defined via the Hamiltonian formalism.
AI.method: Uses the Hamiltonian definition of conserved quantities in TEGR to derive a closed-form expression for the perturbative angular momentum δJ in terms of the axial perturbation function h₀(r,t); analyzes radial and temporal behavior using known axial quasinormal modes of the Bardeen spacetime.
AI.result: Derives an explicit expression for δJ showing a sharp multipolar selection rule: δJ = 0 for odd ℓ, and nonzero for even ℓ; illustrates time- and radius-dependent behavior of δJ using axial quasinormal modes.
AI.conclusion: Axial perturbations of the Bardeen black hole in TEGR carry angular momentum exclusively through even-ℓ multipole modes—a novel selection rule arising from the interplay of regularity, parity, and teleparallel conservation laws.

title: Counting Degrees of Freedom in Open Effective Theories
summary:
Open effective field theories provide a systematic framework for describing physical systems interacting with an environment whose microscopic details are unknown, unobservable, or uncalculable. A basic step in constructing any effective field theory is the identification of the relevant degrees of freedom. For open effective theories, however, this step is subtle: their dynamics is generically dissipative and non-Hamiltonian, so the standard Hamiltonian and Lagrangian algorithms are not directly applicable.
  To overcome this limitation, we develop an algorithm to count degrees of freedom directly from the equations of motion.
