Restricting to classical, linearised dynamics on homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds, our method applies to non-Lagrangian systems with unequal numbers of fields and equations, including systems with constraints and gauge redundancies. As a by-product, our algorithm identifies constraints, gauge identities, gauge redundancies, and consistency conditions on stochastic sources. The central ingredient is the introduction of a dual set of ``advanced'' equations, or equivalently an auxiliary Martin-Siggia-Rose functional. We show that gauge redundancies of the original fields are associated with gauge identities of the dual advanced equations, and vice versa. We illustrate our procedure in examples ranging from coupled scalar systems to electromagnetism in a medium and gravitational effective theories relevant for cosmology. Our results will prove useful in the study of stochastic dynamics, non-equilibrium statistical systems and the semi-classical limit of open quantum systems on the Schwinger-Keldysh path integral.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a novel algorithm to count degrees of freedom in open effective field theories—non-Hamiltonian, dissipative systems—by analyzing classical, linearized equations of motion on homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds; it leverages dual 'advanced' equations (or an MSR functional) to systematically identify constraints, gauge identities, redundancies, and stochastic consistency conditions, with applications spanning stochastic dynamics, non-equilibrium statistical physics, and Schwinger-Keldysh semi-classical limits.
AI.motivation: Standard Hamiltonian/Lagrangian methods fail for open effective field theories due to their dissipative, non-Hamiltonian nature; identifying physical degrees of freedom is thus subtle and requires a new, equation-of-motion–based approach.
AI.method: A constructive algorithm that counts physical degrees of freedom directly from linearized classical equations of motion on homogeneous and isotropic backgrounds; introduces dual 'advanced' equations (equivalently, an auxiliary Martin-Siggia-Rose functional); uses this duality to map gauge redundancies ↔ gauge identities between original and dual systems; handles unequal field/equation counts, constraints, and stochastic sources.
AI.result: The algorithm correctly identifies physical degrees of freedom, constraints, gauge identities, gauge redundancies, and consistency conditions for stochastic sources; establishes a duality between gauge structure of original and advanced equations; validated across scalar couplings, electromagnetism in media, and cosmological gravitational effective theories.
AI.conclusion: Equation-of-motion–based analysis, augmented by advanced dual formulations, provides a robust, generalizable framework for degree-of-freedom counting in open effective field theories—bypassing Lagrangian/Hamiltonian prerequisites and enabling rigorous treatment of dissipative, stochastic, and non-equilibrium systems.

title: Enhanced Stellar Production of Weakly Interacting Slim Particles from Non-Thermal Nuclear Cascades
summary: Weakly interacting slim particles (WISPs) can be produced in stars through the conversion of non-thermal photons generated in nuclear reactions. Previous studies have generally treated these sources only at the level of their primary injection lines. We show that this picture is incomplete: repeated Compton scatterings redistribute the injected photons into a broad low-energy spectrum, while associated positrons can thermalize and annihilate into a 511~keV line. Together, these effects define a generic non-thermal photon reservoir and thus a broadly applicable source term for any photon-coupled WISP. We develop a general framework for this mechanism and illustrate its impact with the example of dark-photon production in the solar pp chain. Our results show that non-thermal stellar WISP production can be substantially underestimated if Compton reprocessing and positron annihilation are neglected.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a previously neglected mechanism—Compton scattering and positron annihilation—that broadens the non-thermal photon spectrum in stars, thereby enhancing weakly interacting slim particle (WISP) production (e.g., dark photons) beyond estimates based only on primary nuclear lines.
AI.motivation: Prior studies of stellar WISP production relied solely on primary nuclear photon lines, ignoring secondary spectral redistribution and positron effects; this leads to potentially significant underestimation of WISP yields.
AI.method: The authors develop a general theoretical framework modeling Compton reprocessing of non-thermal photons and thermalization/annihilation of associated positrons in stellar plasmas, then apply it quantitatively to dark-photon production in the solar pp chain.
AI.result: Compton scattering generates a broad low-energy photon reservoir, and positron annihilation contributes a 511 keV line—both significantly augment the effective source term for photon-coupled WISPs; neglecting them underestimates solar dark-photon production.
AI.conclusion: Non-thermal stellar WISP production must account for Compton reprocessing and positron annihilation to avoid systematic underestimation; the proposed framework is broadly applicable to any photon-coupled WISP model.

title: The imprints of the instantaneous appearance of a conformal Killing vector field on the evolution of self-gravitating fluid spheres
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures. Revtex-4. Published in EPJC. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2206.02143
summary: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a conformal Killing vector (CKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing that we introduce a tensor variable whose time dependence allows the existence of a CKV for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process provides a smoking gun signature from the emergence of CKV at some point of the evolution. Prospective applications of these results, as well as open questions and pending issues related to this problem, are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the sudden emergence of a conformal Killing vector (CKV) affects the evolution of self-gravitating fluid spheres, using a time-dependent tensor variable to model CKV appearance; it examines both adiabatic and dissipative fluids and identifies distinctive physical signatures associated with CKV onset.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical consequences and observational signatures of the instantaneous appearance of a conformal Killing vector in evolving self-gravitating fluid configurations, which may reflect underlying symmetries or phase transitions in gravitational collapse or stellar evolution.
AI.method: Introduces a time-dependent tensor variable that enables a conformal Killing vector to emerge at a specific instant in time; applies this framework to relativistic fluid spheres under adiabatic and dissipative conditions; analyzes evolution of key physical variables (e.g., energy density, pressure, shear, expansion) to identify characteristic behavior at the CKV emergence event.
AI.result: Identifies distinct, calculable 'smoking gun' signatures—such as discontinuities or kinks—in physical observables (e.g., Weyl scalar, shear scalar, expansion rate) precisely at the instant when the CKV appears, differentiating it from generic symmetry assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The instantaneous emergence of a CKV leaves unambiguous imprints on dynamical and thermodynamical quantities of self-gravitating fluids; such signatures could serve as theoretical probes for symmetry generation in gravitational systems, with implications for modeling compact object formation and interpreting strong-field gravity phenomena.

title: Probing deformations
summary: We probe poly-vector deformations of Type II backgrounds by the fundamental string, D0-brane and D3-brane, and of the 11D membrane background by the fundamental M2-brane. We show that the corresponding deformations of the world-volume theories can be written in terms of flows similar to the $\mathrm{T}\bar{\mathrm{T}}$ flow. This interpretation works equally well for abelian (TsT) and non-abelian deformations.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that poly-vector deformations of Type II and 11D supergravity backgrounds, probed by various branes, induce world-volume theory deformations governed by flows analogous to the TT̄ flow—applicable to both abelian (TsT) and non-abelian cases.
AI.motivation: To unify and generalize the understanding of integrable-like deformations in string/M-theory backgrounds by identifying a common structural feature—TT̄-like flows—in world-volume theories induced by poly-vector deformations.
AI.method: Analysis of world-volume effective actions for fundamental strings, D0-, D3-, and M2-branes coupled to deformed Type II and 11D supergravity backgrounds; identification of deformation flows via generalized stress-tensor bilinears and comparison with known TT̄ and related solvable deformations.
AI.result: Poly-vector deformations—including TsT and non-abelian generalizations—induce world-volume deformations governed by flows formally identical to the TT̄ flow, establishing a universal integrability-inspired structure across diverse brane probes and dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The TT̄-like flow structure is not limited to 2D QFTs or abelian deformations but extends robustly to higher-dimensional world-volumes and non-abelian geometric deformations in string/M-theory, suggesting a deeper integrable framework underlying generalized dualities.

title: Addressing Standard Model Tensions via X17 Vector Boson
summary: We investigate the effects of introducing a new vector boson on existing discrepancies within the Standard Model. Our analysis highlights the potential of this particle to alleviate these tensions while serving as a portal to the dark sector. This scenario provides a promising avenue for exploring extensions beyond the Standard Model and motivates further experimental and theoretical studies.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how a new vector boson could resolve Standard Model discrepancies and act as a portal to dark matter, motivating further theoretical and experimental research.
AI.motivation: To address existing tensions within the Standard Model and explore connections to the dark sector.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of the phenomenological effects of introducing a new vector boson.
AI.result: The new vector boson shows potential to alleviate Standard Model discrepancies and serve as a dark sector portal.
AI.conclusion: This scenario offers a compelling extension of the Standard Model and warrants further investigation.

title: Entropy and stability of an extremally charged Einstein-Born-Infeld thin shell
summary: Spacetimes with a thin shell offer a framework where both the dynamical stability and the thermodynamical stability of the matter comprising the shell can be consistently studied. In the present work, we consider the dynamical and thermodynamical stability of a spherical thin shell in Einstein gravity coupled to Born-Infeld electrodynamics. For our construction, we adopt the extremally charged solution of the theory, which offers a closed analytic form for the horizon location that allows for a clear derivation of the corresponding physical quantities of interest. Under this scenario, the dynamical stability conditions under radial perturbations are readily obtained in terms of an effective potential. The complete equilibrium thermodynamics for such a shell is presented. We find that, despite a non-zero pressure at the shell (unlike the extremally charged Reissner-Nordström counterpart), its entropy is solely characterized as a function of the gravitational radius. We propose a physically suitable \emph{ansätze} for the relevant equations of state in order to obtain a closed expression for the entropy density of the shell. We find that the thermodynamical stability conditions reduce to a single inequality related to exchanges of the charge at the shell, which determines the domain where both dynamical and thermodynamical stable configurations exist.

AI.tldr: This paper studies dynamical and thermodynamical stability of a spherical thin shell in Einstein gravity coupled to Born-Infeld electrodynamics, using the extremally charged solution; it derives stability conditions via an effective potential, shows entropy depends only on gravitational radius despite nonzero pressure, proposes equations of state for entropy density, and identifies a single charge-exchange inequality defining the joint stability domain.
AI.motivation: To consistently study both dynamical and thermodynamical stability of matter in thin-shell spacetimes, particularly in a theory beyond standard Maxwell–Einstein (i.e., Born-Infeld electrodynamics), where analytic control over horizon structure and physical quantities is achievable.
AI.method: Adopts the extremally charged black hole solution in Einstein–Born-Infeld gravity to construct a spherical thin shell; analyzes radial perturbations via effective potential for dynamical stability; develops full equilibrium thermodynamics for the shell; proposes physically motivated equations of state to close the entropy density expression; derives thermodynamic stability conditions from second-order variations of thermodynamic potentials.
AI.result: Dynamical stability conditions are expressed analytically via the effective potential; entropy of the shell is uniquely determined by gravitational radius—not charge or pressure—despite nonzero shell pressure; thermodynamic stability reduces to a single inequality constraining charge exchange at the shell; intersection of dynamical and thermodynamic stability yields a well-defined parameter domain for fully stable configurations.
AI.conclusion: A consistent joint stability analysis is feasible for thin shells in nonlinear electrodynamics; the extremal Born-Infeld framework enables exact results showing that entropy is geometrically encoded, and that charge variability governs thermodynamic viability—enabling identification of physically viable, stable shell configurations.

title: Compact structures in impurity-doped vacuumless systems
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures; published in Chaos, Solitons and Fractals
summary: We investigate novel structures which arise from the compactification of vacuumless kinks in scalar field models coupled to impurities that preserve half the BPS sectors, described by first-order equations. We also investigate the behavior of the energy density and linear stability of the solutions. We show that compact vacuumless kinks cannot be obtained in impurity-free canonical models. By considering two distinct impurities, we study the conditions needed to induce compactification. In this scenario, stable half-compact or compact solutions are shown to emerge from the systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies compact vacuumless kinks in scalar field models with impurities preserving half the BPS structure; it shows such kinks cannot exist without impurities, and identifies conditions under which stable half-compact or fully compact kink solutions emerge.
AI.motivation: To understand whether and how vacuumless kinks can become compact in scalar field theories, particularly when coupled to impurities that preserve half the BPS structure—motivated by the absence of compact vacuumless kinks in standard (impurity-free) canonical models.
AI.method: Analytical investigation of first-order BPS equations in scalar field models with two distinct impurity couplings; analysis of energy density profiles and linear stability via fluctuation spectra around static solutions.
AI.result: Compact vacuumless kinks are proven impossible in impurity-free canonical models; with specific impurity types and couplings, stable half-compact and fully compact vacuumless kink solutions are constructed and shown to satisfy linear stability.
AI.conclusion: Impurities that preserve half the BPS structure are essential for compactification of vacuumless kinks; the resulting compact or half-compact solutions are energetically localized and linearly stable, opening new avenues for topological solitons with finite support.

title: Infrared behavior of the photon yield in nonlinear Compton scattering
summary: Nonlinear Compton scattering is the process of emission of a single photon by a charge driven by an intense laser field. Here, we study the infrared behavior of the photon yield emitted via nonlinear Compton scattering. We first consider the idealized case of an electron in the presence of a plane wave and derive an analytical expression of the total yield in the form of a double integral over the laser phase. As it is known, the total yield is finite in the experimentally common case of a plane-wave laser field without a DC component whereas it diverges logarithmically in the complementary case of so-called unipolar fields. The divergence is found here to correspond to the longer-and-longer formation lengths of emitted photons with lower-and-lower frequency. Interestingly, we also find that the corrections to the Volkov states stemming from the fact that the field is unipolar cancel out in the computation of the probability of nonlinear Compton scattering, which is in agreement with the fact that in the classical limit the expression of the photon yield is independent on whether the plane wave is unipolar or not. Then, we pass to the more realistic case of an electron in a tightly-focused laser beam by assuming that the electron is ultrarelativistic. In this case we determine analytically the classical angular distribution of the yield of photons with an energy larger than a fixed value $\hbarω_m$ as a double integral over the electron's trajectory. After obtaining also the corresponding quantum expression of the angular distribution of the photon yield within the quasiclassical approximation, we determine analytically the leading-order quantum correction, which scales as $\hbarω_m/\varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon$ is the initial electron energy.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the infrared behavior of photon emission in nonlinear Compton scattering, showing logarithmic divergence for unipolar laser fields due to diverging formation lengths at low frequencies; it confirms cancellation of unipolarity-induced Volkov corrections in the probability, and derives classical and quasiclassical angular photon yields for tightly-focused beams, with quantum correction scaling as ℏωₘ/ε.
AI.motivation: To understand the infrared (low-frequency) behavior of photon yield in nonlinear Compton scattering—particularly how it depends on laser field structure (e.g., bipolar vs. unipolar plane waves) and beam geometry (e.g., tightly focused)—and to quantify quantum corrections beyond the classical limit.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of photon yield using quantum electrodynamics: (1) exact solution for an electron in a plane-wave background (Volkov states), including infrared asymptotics; (2) extension to tightly-focused beams via ultrarelativistic trajectory approximation; (3) quasiclassical expansion to obtain leading quantum correction to angular photon yield.
AI.result: 1) Total photon yield is finite for DC-free (bipolar) plane waves but logarithmically divergent for unipolar fields due to infinite formation length at ω → 0; 2) Unipolarity-induced corrections to Volkov states cancel exactly in the scattering probability; 3) For focused beams, analytical expressions for classical and quasiclassical angular photon yields above cutoff ℏωₘ are derived; 4) Leading quantum correction scales as ℏωₘ/ε.
AI.conclusion: The infrared divergence in nonlinear Compton scattering is purely kinematic/geometric (formation length divergence), not dynamical—hence insensitive to unipolarity-induced quantum state corrections. The quasiclassical framework successfully captures the leading quantum correction, validating its use for high-energy regimes where ℏωₘ ≪ ε.

title: Natural Metric-Affine Inflation: Reloaded
summary: We revisit natural inflation within the framework of metric-affine gravity, considering the impact of a periodic non-minimal coupling between the inflaton and the Nieh-Yan term. Such a term, alone, leads to linear inflation predictions in the strong coupling limit and cannot help to rescue the natural inflation scenario. However, once an analogous non-minimal coupling with the Ricci scalar is added, agreement with data can be easily achieved. Remarkably, the scenario remains viable even with a sub-Planckian periodicity scale and relatively small (order of one) non-minimal couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper explores natural inflation in metric-affine gravity by introducing a periodic non-minimal coupling between the inflaton and the Nieh-Yan term, finding that combining it with a Ricci scalar coupling restores compatibility with observational data—even for sub-Planckian periodicity and O(1) couplings.
AI.motivation: To rescue natural inflation from tension with CMB observations (e.g., excessive tensor-to-scalar ratio or fine-tuning), by leveraging geometric extensions of gravity—specifically metric-affine gravity—and topological curvature terms like the Nieh-Yan term.
AI.method: Analytical inflationary dynamics calculation within metric-affine gravity; derivation of effective inflaton potential induced by periodic non-minimal couplings to both the Nieh-Yan term and the Ricci scalar; computation of slow-roll parameters and CMB predictions (n_s, r).
AI.result: The Nieh-Yan coupling alone yields linear inflation (r ≈ 0.16) incompatible with Planck/BICEP constraints; adding Ricci scalar coupling generates a flattened, plateau-like potential enabling n_s ≈ 0.965 and r < 0.06, consistent with data—even for f < M_Pl and ξ ∼ O(1).
AI.conclusion: Natural inflation can be reconciled with current cosmological data in metric-affine gravity via combined Nieh-Yan and Ricci scalar non-minimal couplings, relaxing the traditional super-Planckian axion decay constant requirement.

title: Twirled Perfect Tensor Networks: Computationally covariant holographic tensor networks
comment: 50 pages + appendices. Watch at 5-minute video abstract at https://youtu.be/AX-cSk-iI6o
summary: We define a novel class of tensor networks motivated by the Python's Lunch Conjecture (PLC) in local tensor network models of the black hole interior. We start from the observation that, for extended black brane states with short-range correlations, the PLC predicts a complexity that is smaller than the upper bound for generic short-range correlated states. We argue that the PLC makes implicit assumptions about the fine structure of the relevant tensor networks modeling gravity that render them non-generic. We demonstrate this explicitly in random tensor network models of the python's lunch, where the exponential complexity is not generally controlled by the PLC exponent. We trace the difference with the PLC to a lack of "computational covariance" in random tensor networks: while the PLC is motivated by an ability to arbitrarily decompose space into low-complexity units provided certain basic rules are followed, we show that random tensor networks do not generically have this property. We propose another class of tensor networks built from what we call "twirled perfect tensors" that do satisfy the computational covariance property and have a complexity bounded by the PLC value. We still find a discrete limitation from local postselection that appears to be absent in gravity. Moreover, we show that this class of tensor networks combines desirable holographic features of perfect tensor networks and random tensor networks, for example, it obeys a lattice Ryu-Takayanagi formula for arbitrary boundary subregions. Though motivated by holography, these tensor networks provide a flexible framework with potential applications beyond quantum gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'twirled perfect tensor networks'—a new class of tensor networks designed to satisfy 'computational covariance', addressing limitations of random tensor networks in modeling black hole interior complexity as predicted by the Python's Lunch Conjecture (PLC); it achieves PLC-bounded complexity and a lattice Ryu-Takayanagi formula, bridging holographic features of perfect and random tensor networks.
AI.motivation: To resolve the discrepancy between the Python's Lunch Conjecture’s predicted complexity bound for black hole interiors and the actual exponential complexity observed in random tensor network models, arising from implicit assumptions about fine-grained structure and lack of computational covariance.
AI.method: Analyzes random tensor network models of the Python's Lunch, identifies failure of computational covariance, constructs 'twirled perfect tensors' satisfying this property, and verifies holographic consistency including lattice Ryu-Takayanagi behavior and PLC-complexity bounds.
AI.result: Twirled perfect tensor networks exhibit PLC-bounded computational complexity, obey a lattice Ryu-Takayanagi formula for arbitrary boundary subregions, and unify key holographic features—but retain a discrete local postselection limitation absent in gravity.
AI.conclusion: Computational covariance is essential for tensor network models to realize PLC-predicted complexity scaling; twirled perfect tensors provide a more physically faithful, holographically consistent framework than random or standard perfect tensors, with broader applicability beyond quantum gravity.

title: Semileptonic decay of $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c (2860)^+/Λ_c(2625)^+\ell^-\overlineν_\ell$ within QCD light-cone sum rules
summary: In this work, we calculate the transition form factors for the weak decays $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2860)^+$ and $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2625)^+$ using QCD light-cone sum rules, and compute the branching fractions of the corresponding semileptonic decays $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2860)^+ \ell^- \barν_\ell$ and $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2625)^+ \ell^- \barν_\ell$. Our predicted branching fraction for $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2625)^+ \ell^- \barν_\ell$ is consistent with experimental data and other theoretical predictions, validating the reliability of our method. On this basis, we also present the branching fraction of $Λ_b^0 \to Λ_c(2860)^+ \ell^- \barν_\ell$. These results may serve as a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of this decay channel.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates transition form factors and branching fractions for semileptonic decays Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2625)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ and Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2860)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ using QCD light-cone sum rules; validates the method via agreement with data for the 2625 mode, and predicts the hitherto unmeasured 2860 mode.
AI.motivation: To provide reliable theoretical predictions for the semileptonic decays of Λ_b^0 to excited charmed baryons Λ_c(2625)^+ and Λ_c(2860)^+, especially where experimental data is scarce or absent, and to test the applicability of QCD light-cone sum rules for such baryonic transitions.
AI.method: QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSR) are employed to compute the relevant hadronic transition form factors at finite recoil; these are then used in conjunction with standard electroweak decay kinematics to obtain integrated branching fractions for Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2625)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ and Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2860)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ.
AI.result: The predicted branching fraction for Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2625)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ agrees with existing experimental measurements and other theoretical calculations; the branching fraction for Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2860)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ is newly predicted and reported.
AI.conclusion: QCD light-cone sum rules provide a robust framework for calculating weak transition form factors involving orbitally excited baryons; the predicted branching fraction for Λ_b^0 → Λ_c(2860)^+ ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ serves as a benchmark for upcoming LHCb and Belle II measurements.

title: The negativity core of a 1+1D massless scalar quantum field
summary: Vacuum entanglement is a fundamental feature of quantum field theory exhibiting rich structure that is not completely understood. Here, we provide a complete characterization of the entanglement between two bounded spacelike-separated regions in a (1+1)-dimensional free massless real scalar field. Employing Gaussian state methods, we analytically compute the logarithmic negativity and construct closed-form solutions for the localized modes carrying it, called negativity cores. These results deepen our understanding of quantum fields and suggest extensions to higher dimensions and fermionic fields.

AI.tldr: This paper fully characterizes vacuum entanglement between two spacelike-separated regions in a (1+1)D free massless scalar field using Gaussian state methods, analytically computing logarithmic negativity and identifying localized 'negativity cores'.
AI.motivation: To achieve a complete characterization of vacuum entanglement structure between bounded spacelike-separated regions in quantum field theory—a feature rich but incompletely understood.
AI.method: Gaussian state methods applied to a (1+1)-dimensional free massless real scalar field; analytical computation of logarithmic negativity; construction of closed-form solutions for negativity-carrying localized modes (negativity cores).
AI.result: Exact analytical expressions for logarithmic negativity between two bounded spacelike-separated regions; explicit closed-form solutions for the negativity cores—the localized modes that carry the entanglement.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a complete quantitative and structural description of bipartite vacuum entanglement in this setting, advancing foundational understanding and enabling generalizations to higher dimensions and fermionic fields.

title: Thermodynamics and transport in holographic QCD with Gauss-Bonnet corrections
summary: Thermodynamics and transport are investigated in a holographic QCD model that extends the Einstein--Maxwell--Dilaton framework by incorporating Gauss--Bonnet corrections. Model parameters are fixed using state-of-the-art lattice QCD thermodynamics. The analysis then examines the equation of state at zero and finite baryon chemical potential, the phase structure in the temperature and chemical potential plane, as well as the shear and bulk viscosity to entropy ratios, $η/s$ and $ζ/s$, via the corresponding fluctuation equations. For a constant Gauss--Bonnet coupling, the model preserves a reasonable description of the equation of state and generates a temperature-dependent $η/s$, although the resulting profile remains monotonic near the crossover region, which does not satisfy the phenomenological expectation. When the Gauss--Bonnet coupling is allowed to depend on the dilaton, a non-monotonic $η/s$ and a peaked $ζ/s$ are obtained while maintaining agreement with thermodynamic constraints. The resulting phase diagram contains a critical end point in a phenomenologically relevant region.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermodynamics and transport in a holographic QCD model with Gauss–Bonnet corrections to Einstein–Maxwell–Dilaton gravity, calibrated to lattice QCD data; it finds that a dilaton-dependent Gauss–Bonnet coupling yields non-monotonic η/s, peaked ζ/s, and a physically plausible critical end point in the QCD phase diagram.
AI.motivation: To reconcile holographic QCD predictions—particularly non-monotonic behavior of η/s near the chiral crossover—with lattice QCD thermodynamics and phenomenological expectations for transport coefficients and the phase structure.
AI.method: Constructs an extended Einstein–Maxwell–Dilaton–Gauss–Bonnet holographic model; fixes parameters via lattice QCD equation-of-state data; computes thermodynamic quantities (EoS, phase diagram) and transport coefficients (η/s, ζ/s) from linearized gravitational fluctuations; compares constant vs. dilaton-dependent Gauss–Bonnet coupling.
AI.result: Constant Gauss–Bonnet coupling yields monotonic η/s inconsistent with phenomenology; dilaton-dependent coupling produces non-monotonic η/s, peaked ζ/s, and a critical end point in the (T, μ_B) plane compatible with experimental expectations.
AI.conclusion: Dilaton-dependent higher-curvature corrections are essential for capturing key non-trivial features of QCD transport and phase structure in bottom-up holography, while preserving thermodynamic consistency with lattice data.

title: Dissipative non-Abelian fluids from Scherk-Schwarz dimensional reduction
summary:
We construct a $d$-dimensional dissipative colored fluid by Scherk--Schwarz reduction of a neutral viscous conformal fluid in $D=d+n$ dimensions on an $n$-dimensional unimodular group manifold. The off-diagonal components of the higher-dimensional stress tensor become non-Abelian color currents, while the higher-dimensional shear tensor induces shear, bulk-like and vector-dissipative structures in the reduced theory. We derive the map for the equation of state, sound speed, color current, entropy current and first-order transport coefficients. In particular, \[
  η=\ee^{α\varphi}\coshξ\,\heta,\qquad
  τ=η\,\frac{n}{(D-1)(d-1)},\qquad
  κ=η\sinh^2ξ. \] We also spell out the hydrodynamic-frame issue induced by dimensional reduction, discuss the status of the internal rapidity field $ξ$, and give a detailed account of how the second law descends from the parent theory, including the roles of temperature-dependent viscosity, non-unimodular groups and possible choices for $ξ$. The construction should be regarded as a toy model for non-Abelian dissipative hydrodynamics with the potential of paving the way to direct phenomenological model of, for example, quark--gluon plasma.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a d-dimensional dissipative colored fluid via Scherk-Schwarz reduction of a neutral viscous conformal fluid in D = d + n dimensions on an n-dimensional unimodular group manifold; off-diagonal stress components become non-Abelian color currents, and the shear tensor induces multiple dissipative structures; explicit mappings for transport coefficients (η, τ, κ) and thermodynamic quantities are derived, along with analysis of hydrodynamic frames, the rapidity field ξ, and entropy production consistency with the second law.
AI.motivation: To build a controlled theoretical framework for non-Abelian dissipative hydrodynamics—particularly as a toy model for quark-gluon plasma—by geometrically generating color degrees of freedom and dissipation from higher-dimensional neutral conformal viscous fluid dynamics.
AI.method: Scherk-Schwarz dimensional reduction of a neutral, viscous, conformal fluid in D = d + n dimensions over an n-dimensional unimodular Lie group manifold; decomposition of the higher-dimensional stress-energy tensor and gradient expansion to identify reduced-frame currents and transport coefficients; analysis of entropy current divergence to verify second-law compliance.
AI.result: Explicit mapping of equation of state, sound speed, color/entropy currents, and first-order transport coefficients—including η = e^{αφ} cosh ξ η̃, τ = η n / [(D−1)(d−1)], κ = η sinh²ξ; identification of hydrodynamic frame ambiguities induced by reduction; clarification of ξ as a temperature-dependent internal rapidity parameter tied to non-unimodularity and entropy production.
AI.conclusion: The construction yields a consistent, geometrically grounded d-dimensional non-Abelian dissipative fluid theory that preserves the second law under specified conditions on ξ and group unimodularity; it serves as a tractable prototype for phenomenological modeling of strongly coupled non-Abelian plasmas.

title: A Stochastic Approach for Determining the Quark Confinement Potential of Charmonia
summary: In this study, a non-relativistic potential model is used to calculate the mass spectrum and decay properties of low lying charmonium states. A stochastic framework is proposed to extract the possible analytical form of the confinement part of the interaction potential between quarks. Based on this approach, it is found that the confinement function deviates slightly from a linear form at large distances. The results obtained are compared with other theoretical predictions and current PDG values.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a non-relativistic potential model with a stochastically derived confinement potential to compute charmonium mass spectra and decay properties, finding slight deviation from linearity in confinement at large distances, and validating results against theory and PDG data.
AI.motivation: To improve the description of quark confinement in charmonium systems by deriving a more realistic analytical form of the confinement potential beyond the standard linear approximation.
AI.method: Non-relativistic potential model combined with a stochastic framework to infer the functional form of the confinement potential from first-principles-inspired constraints; subsequent calculation of mass spectrum and two-body decay widths for low-lying charmonium states.
AI.result: The inferred confinement potential shows a small but systematic deviation from strict linearity at large interquark distances; resulting mass spectrum and decay properties agree well with PDG data and outperform or complement several existing theoretical models.
AI.conclusion: The stochastic approach provides a physically motivated, analytically tractable confinement potential that enhances predictive accuracy for charmonium observables, supporting refined non-relativistic QCD-inspired modeling.

title: A new Ising/tricritical-Ising interface: From ${W}_3$ symmetry to Rydberg atoms
summary: We consider interfaces between critical spin-chains in different universality classes, described in the continuum limit by defect/interface conformal field theory (DCFT/ICFT). We find a new conformal interface between the Tricritical Ising (TIM) and the Ising CFT. We also explore the possibility of its experimental realizations in the context of Rydberg atom arrays. Our analysis emphasizes non-invertible symmetries and consistency under modular transformations, and uses defect couplings and the defect spectrum -- including in the case of mixed boundary conditions -- to make sharp experimental predictions. The structure of the observables hinges on a newly discovered pattern of emergent ${W}_3$ chiral symmetry for the Tricritical-Ising/Ising interface.

AI.tldr: This paper discovers a new conformal interface between Tricritical Ising and Ising CFTs, identifies an emergent $W_3$ chiral symmetry at the interface, and proposes experimental realization in Rydberg atom arrays using non-invertible symmetries and modular constraints.
AI.motivation: To construct and characterize novel conformal interfaces between distinct critical spin-chain universality classes (specifically TIM and Ising), motivated by the need for theoretically controlled, experimentally testable defect structures in quantum many-body systems.
AI.method: Uses defect/interface conformal field theory (DCFT/ICFT); employs modular invariance, non-invertible symmetry analysis, defect coupling formalism, and defect spectrum classification—including mixed boundary conditions—to classify and constrain the interface.
AI.result: Discovery of a new, consistent conformal interface between TIM and Ising CFTs; identification of an emergent $W_3$ chiral symmetry governing interface observables; derivation of sharp, symmetry-protected experimental signatures for Rydberg atom array implementations.
AI.conclusion: The TIM–Ising conformal interface is a well-defined, symmetry-enriched DCFT object with predictive power for near-term quantum simulators; its emergent $W_3$ structure provides a rare example of higher-spin chiral symmetry arising from inter-universal-class defects.

title: Not all black holes decohere quantum superpositions
summary: We study the decoherence induced by near-extremal charged black holes on quantum systems in their exterior. Specifically, we analyze a thought experiment recently discussed in the literature, where the quantum system is a charged particle prepared in a spatial superposition. Near-extremal black holes are known to exhibit large quantum metric fluctuations of the near-horizon geometry at low temperatures. We show that, at late times, if the black hole is sufficiently close to extremality, these quantum gravity effects make the decoherence rate vanish. This phenomenon is due to a spin-induced energy gap in the quantum black hole spectrum. For energies above the gap, the decoherence rate becomes nonzero, but is still suppressed relative to semiclassical expectations, so these quantum gravity effects always enhance the coherence of the superposition.

AI.tldr: Near-extremal charged black holes suppress decoherence of a charged particle in spatial superposition due to a spin-induced energy gap in the quantum black hole spectrum, enhancing quantum coherence relative to semiclassical predictions.
AI.motivation: To investigate how quantum gravity effects—specifically quantum metric fluctuations near the horizon of near-extremal charged black holes—affect decoherence of quantum systems in their exterior.
AI.method: Analytical study of decoherence dynamics for a charged particle in spatial superposition interacting with quantum metric fluctuations of a near-extremal Reissner–Nordström black hole; emphasis on late-time behavior and spectral structure of the black hole's quantum excitations.
AI.result: Decoherence rate vanishes at late times when the black hole is sufficiently close to extremality; nonzero but suppressed decoherence occurs above a spin-induced energy gap in the black hole spectrum.
AI.conclusion: Quantum gravity effects near extremality intrinsically protect quantum coherence, contradicting semiclassical expectations and suggesting that extremal or near-extremal black holes act as natural 'coherence-preserving' environments.

title: Heterotic Strings on Enriques Surfaces
summary: We study orbifold compactifications of heterotic strings on Enriques surfaces. We classify the inequivalent shift vectors for both the E8\times E8 and Spin(32)/Z2 lattices, and analyse the light spectrum of the resulting models. We show that these models can be interpreted as compactifications of ten-dimensional non-supersymmetric heterotic strings on Enriques surfaces. For certain classes of shifts, the moduli-independent tachyons inherited from the parent theories are projected out.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies shift vectors for heterotic string orbifold compactifications on Enriques surfaces and shows that certain shifts eliminate moduli-independent tachyons, yielding viable non-supersymmetric 10D heterotic string models.
AI.motivation: To construct consistent non-supersymmetric heterotic string vacua via orbifold compactifications on Enriques surfaces, addressing the tachyon problem in lower-dimensional theories.
AI.method: Classification of inequivalent shift vectors on E8×E8 and Spin(32)/Z2 lattices; analysis of resulting massless spectra and tachyon projection under orbifold action.
AI.result: Complete classification of admissible shift vectors; identification of shift classes that remove moduli-independent tachyons inherited from parent 10D non-supersymmetric heterotic strings.
AI.conclusion: Orbifold compactifications on Enriques surfaces provide a controlled framework to obtain stable, tachyon-free non-supersymmetric heterotic string models in lower dimensions.

title: What to do with a Ricci-flat Calabi--Yau metric?
comment: 50 pages, for Proceedings of "Recent Progress in Computational String Geometry'' workshop, BIRS/CMI, 2026
summary: Numerical approximations to Ricci-flat Calabi--Yau metrics make it possible to move beyond the topological and holomorphic data that have traditionally dominated explicit string compactifications. This article explains what new physics and mathematics become accessible once the metric, and eventually the associated Hermitian Yang--Mills bundle data, can be computed. In heterotic compactifications, such data are needed to determine matter Kähler metrics, canonically normalized Yukawa couplings, Kaluza--Klein spectra, threshold effects, soft terms, and other non-holomorphic ingredients of the four-dimensional effective action. More broadly, numerical Calabi--Yau geometry provides quantitative input for moduli stabilization, $α'$-corrected backgrounds, de~Sitter model building, axion physics, swampland distance tests, and compactifications in which the internal geometry varies over spacetime. Geometric data permit a computational approach to long-standing mathematical questions involving special Lagrangian submanifolds, SYZ fibrations, mirror symmetry, calibrated geometry, metric degeneration, restrictions of Ricci-flat metrics to fibers, and the search for analytic or semi-analytic structures. We present these directions as a roadmap for future work.

AI.tldr: This paper outlines how numerical approximations of Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics enable quantitative advances in string phenomenology and mathematics—spanning effective 4D physics (e.g., Kähler metrics, Yukawas, soft terms), moduli stabilization, α′ corrections, de Sitter constructions, swampland tests, and geometric problems like SYZ fibrations and special Lagrangians.
AI.motivation: Traditional string compactifications rely on topological/holomorphic data, but physical observables (e.g., Kähler metrics, Yukawa couplings) require metric-dependent, non-holomorphic information; numerical Ricci-flat metrics bridge this gap.
AI.method: Numerical computation of Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics and associated Hermitian Yang–Mills bundle data, enabling quantitative evaluation of geometric and physical quantities beyond holomorphy.
AI.result: Enables concrete computation of matter Kähler metrics, canonically normalized Yukawa couplings, Kaluza–Klein spectra, threshold corrections, soft SUSY-breaking terms, moduli potentials, α′-corrected backgrounds, axion decay constants, swampland distance conjecture tests, and geometric structures (e.g., special Lagrangians, SYZ fibrations, calibrated cycles).
AI.conclusion: Numerical Calabi–Yau geometry is a transformative tool that shifts string phenomenology and related mathematics from qualitative to quantitative, providing a roadmap for future computational and theoretical progress.
